a141.speaker: Kano State government (court suit)
a141.name: Kano State government (court suit)
a141.speech: Has filed a suit before the State High Court, seeking to reclaim its 20 percent equity stake in Dala Inland Dry Port Limited and recover funds allegedly misappropriated to the tune of ₦4,492,387,013.76; the case was filed on October 13, 2025.

a141.speaker: Charge sheet (Kano State High Court)
a141.name: Charge sheet (Kano State High Court)
a141.speech: According to the charge sheet, the defendants allegedly conspired to fraudulently transfer 80 percent shares of Dala Inland Dry Port, including the state government’s 20 percent equity, to private entities under the fictitious name “City Green Enterprise” to conceal the true ownership of the company; the defendants face a 10-count charge bordering on criminal conspiracy, misappropriation of public funds, breach of trust, and conflict of interest.

a141.speaker: The prosecution
a141.name: The prosecution
a141.speech: Alleged that the defendants diverted over ₦4.49billion of Kano State funds to execute infrastructure projects such as a double carriageway, electricity, and perimeter fencing at the dry port for their personal and family benefit; accused them of abuse of office and conflict of interest, with claims that they used their official positions to manipulate public resources for private gains, in violation of financial and constitutional regulations.

a141.speaker: The prosecution (summary of evidence)
a141.name: The prosecution (summary of evidence)
a141.speech: Alleged that the defendants used sham entities and proxies to hide ownership of the Dala Inland Dry Port shares, diverted public funds to family-owned firms and personal businesses, coerced the original project founders into relinquishing control while allowing them to retain only nominal shares, created false documents and misleading letters to deceive regulatory authorities, and orchestrated a chain of transactions, including through Safari Textile Ltd (STL Enterprise), to facilitate the diversion of ₦750million in state funds; has lined up several key witnesses to testify in court, including the lead investigating officer who uncovered the alleged fraudulent transactions and an early stakeholder in the project.

a345.speaker: Mpho Balopi, former Cabinet minister and principal of Walgreen Investments (submissions to the High Court)
a345.name: Mpho Balopi
a345.title: former Cabinet minister and principal of Walgreen Investments (submissions to the High Court)
a345.speech: The explosive allegations are contained in Balopi's submissions to the High Court made on Wednesday; Balopi alleges that the Agriculture minister made good faith representations, saying the matter between Balopi's company, Walgreen Investments and the BMC should be resolved amicably and without resort to courts.

a345.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Botswana (as alleged in Balopi's court submissions)
a345.name: Minister of Agriculture of Botswana (as alleged in Balopi's court submissions)
a345.speech: Made good faith representations, saying the matter between Walgreen Investments and the BMC should be resolved amicably and without resort to courts.

a345.speaker: Tebogo Tladi, Balopi's attorney
a345.name: Tebogo Tladi
a345.title: Balopi's attorney
a345.speech: On Wednesday filed papers before court opposing the BMC's recent award of a stay of execution, in the matter in which the assets were seized from the parastatal's Lobatse headquarters.

a388.speaker: World Bank (interim damage assessment report, produced with the United Nations and the European Union)
a388.name: World Bank (interim damage assessment report
a388.title: produced with the United Nations and the European Union)
a388.speech: Says the Israel-Hamas war has caused damage of around $18.5 billion to Gaza's critical infrastructure, equivalent to 97% of the combined economic output of the West Bank and Gaza in 2022; found structural damage affected "every sector of the economy," with more than 70% of the estimated costs due to the destruction of housing. "For several sectors, the rate of damage appears to be levelling off as few assets remain intact." ; Found that more than half of Gaza's population were on the brink of famine, with the whole population "experiencing acute food insecurity and malnutrition"; that an estimated 84% of Gaza's health facilities have been damaged or destroyed, three quarters of the population displaced, Gaza's water and sanitation system had "nearly collapsed" and was delivering less than 5% of its pre-war output, 100% of Gaza's children were out of school and 92% of its primary roads were destroyed or damaged.

a388.speaker: World Bank (report recommendations)
a388.name: World Bank (report recommendations)
a388.speech: The report called for "an increase in humanitarian assistance, food aid and food production; the provision of shelter and rapid, cost-effective, and scalable housing solutions for displaced people; and the resumption of essential services."

a388.speaker: AFP tally of Israeli official figures
a388.name: AFP tally of Israeli official figures
a388.speech: Cited as the source that Hamas's 7 October attack resulted in about 1,160 mostly civilian deaths in Israel.

a388.speaker: Health ministry in Hamas-run Gaza
a388.name: Health ministry in Hamas-run Gaza
a388.speech: Cited as the source that Israel's retaliatory campaign has killed at least 32,916 people, mostly women and children.

a636.speaker: Government of Liberia
a636.name: Government of Liberia
a636.speech: Says it is resolved to address the gap created by the recent cancellation of USAID-funded projects through the implementation of fiscal reforms and policy measures ; says it will engage in fiscal targeting to minimize losses and reduce waste, and is engaging new partners and exploring regional cooperation within ECOWAS, the EU, and other blocs.

a636.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Liberian Finance Minister
a636.name: Augustine Ngafuan
a636.title: Liberian Finance Minister
a636.speech: Recalls that he recently issued fiscal rules to streamline government expenditures and wrote to ministries and agencies urging them to prioritize their priorities; says that while over US$50 million in USAID-funded projects have been canceled, the government is implementing domestic regulations and measures to bridge the gap while also engaging the international community to explore solutions, noting that some of the projects ran up to 2029, including building primary schools and modern complexes across six counties: “We have submitted our report to President Boakai and are also presenting it to the legislature, outlining the short- and long-term impacts as well as our planned response” ; “USAID was helping us navigate that, but there are other things we are doing to make sure that what we do for ourselves can compensate for the aid withdrawal.” He emphasizes the need to engage partners and increase domestic resource mobilization, and assures that government remains committed to managing the country's economic situation through measures and strategic decisions.

a636.speaker: Dr. Francien Chenoweth Richardson, political commentator
a636.name: Dr. Francien Chenoweth Richardson
a636.title: political commentator
a636.speech: “We expect a strategic plan and solution-based recommendation from Finance Minister Ngafuan.”

a646.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a646.name: Pedro Sánchez
a646.title: Spanish Prime Minister
a646.speech: described Spain’s relationship with Mauritania as “the most ambitious” among Spain’s bilateral partnerships, emphasising the significance of his visit with a high-level ministerial delegation: “This strong representation reflects our firm intention to continue strengthening our ties and to extend cooperation into many other areas.” ; highlighted the breadth of the cooperation agenda, moving beyond the traditional focus on fishing and development assistance: “Our relationship is growing in importance in areas such as the economy, business, migration, security, and culture,” noting the recent opening of a Cervantes Institute branch in Nouakchott and the deep historical ties between Mauritania and the Canary Islands ; welcomed the decision by both governments to elevate their economic partnership, including a Mauritania-Spain Business Council and the ratification of a Treaty of Friendship, Good Neighbourliness, and Cooperation, and announced the conclusion of a business forum held that same day ; emphasised the two countries’ “shared strategic vision” for addressing common challenges across the Mediterranean, Southern Europe, the Sahel, the Maghreb, and the Atlantic, saying this strategic alignment is key to securing the well-being of both societies, and reaffirmed Mauritania’s pivotal role in regional stability and Spain’s support for it.

a646.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a646.name: Pedro Sánchez
a646.title: Spanish Prime Minister
a646.speech: Addressing the issue of migration, drew on Spain’s own experience in emigration and migrant reception, calling for collaboration with countries like Mauritania to ensure “safe, regular, and orderly migration that benefits both societies.”

a646.speaker: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani, Mauritanian President
a646.name: Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani
a646.title: Mauritanian President
a646.speech: recalled that the summit builds on the cooperation agreement signed two years ago, which frames collaboration in both the public and private sectors, and described relations with Spain as “excellent,” grounded in “historical ties and deep friendship between our peoples.” ; expressed his gratitude to Spain for its “steadfast support,” both bilaterally and within the European Union and other international forums, applauding Madrid’s defense of “just causes and global security” ; noted that this first high-level summit enabled both sides to tackle major shared challenges — particularly in security, development, migration, environment, and renewable energy — while welcoming the tangible results and new cooperation frameworks established during the meeting.

a646.speaker: Spain’s annual national security report
a646.name: Spain’s annual national security report
a646.speech: According to the report, Mauritania became in 2024 the leading country of departure for irregular migrants to Spain, with over 25,000 departures — surpassing combined figures from Morocco and Algeria; a total of 61,372 migrants reached Spain via sea routes that year, a new record exceeding that of 2018, and representing a 10.3% increase from 2023.

a646.speaker: Tawassoul (Mauritanian media outlet)
a646.name: Tawassoul (Mauritanian media outlet)
a646.speech: reported that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez arrived in Mauritania on Wednesday, 16 July, for a two-day official visit at the head of a major government and business delegation.

a667.speaker: Senior administration officials familiar with the process (anonymous)
a667.name: Senior administration officials familiar with the process (anonymous)
a667.speech: Said the World Bank's support is not part of the DAG financing, as its officials are in talks with the government for financial support packages separately, with discussions in progress between Ethiopian authorities and the Bank over additional budget support of up to three billion dollars, yet to be approved by the Board of Directors.

a667.speaker: Development Assistance Group (DAG), jointly chaired by the World Bank and Sweden
a667.name: Development Assistance Group (DAG)
a667.title: jointly chaired by the World Bank and Sweden
a667.speech: Confirmed the three-billion-dollar financing package on Friday, December 13, 2019.

a667.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a667.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a667.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a667.speech: Describes the reform as a "pro-job, pro-growth, and pro-inclusivity pathway to prosperity."

a667.speaker: Yinager Dessie (PhD), Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia, and Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), State Minister for Finance
a667.name: Yinager Dessie (PhD)
a667.title: Governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia, and Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), State Minister for Finance
a667.speech: Made a joint appeal in September to the international community to foot part of the bill for the reform package, which is estimated to cost 10 billion dollars.

a667.speaker: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.name: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD)
a667.title: Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.speech: "The development agencies have started to respond to our calls for help."

a667.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), brief statement issued last week
a667.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a667.title: brief statement issued last week
a667.speech: Said the loan, through its dual extended credit and fund facilities, will be provided to address the foreign exchange shortage, strengthen the management of state-owned enterprises and contain debt vulnerabilities; it is also meant to enhance domestic revenue mobilisation, reform the financial sector, and strengthen the government's supervisory role and financial safety nets ; the statement said the loan aspires to help Ethiopia make the "transition to a more flexible exchange rate regime."

a667.speaker: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD), macroeconomist
a667.name: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD)
a667.title: macroeconomist
a667.speech: Said the series of fundings show that these agencies have developed trust and confidence in the reform plan: "This can bring a paradigm shift in the economy." ; "It's an extremely good opportunity for Ethiopia."

a667.speaker: Getachew T. Alemu, economist and consultant
a667.name: Getachew T. Alemu
a667.title: economist and consultant
a667.speech: Cautioned that the latest window of help from the IMF signals the severe balance of payments crisis in the economy, citing the IMF's noninvolvement in development financing: "The help shows the country needed an external interjection to solve its balance of payments crisis."

a667.speaker: Getachew T. Alemu, economist and consultant
a667.name: Getachew T. Alemu
a667.title: economist and consultant
a667.speech: Believes the support will build trust in other international agencies toward Ethiopia: "Once they see the IMF puts money into Ethiopia, others will be confident investing in the economy."

a667.speaker: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.name: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD)
a667.title: Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.speech: "We're negotiating with Middle East countries, including Saudi Arabia, for loan restructuring and rescheduling."

a667.speaker: Alemayehu Geda (prof.), macroeconomist lecturing at Addis Abeba University
a667.name: Alemayehu Geda (prof.)
a667.title: macroeconomist lecturing at Addis Abeba University
a667.speech: Believes the Homegrown Economic Reform Programme is "basically an IMF/WB policy" ; tweeted recently, in response to news of the IMF's plan to provide loans for Ethiopia: "The IMF and our government don't seem to care about the inflationary consequence of their devaluation policy, which hurts the poor most."

a667.speaker: Getachew T. Alemu, economist and consultant
a667.name: Getachew T. Alemu
a667.title: economist and consultant
a667.speech: Said the transition may lead to the exchange rate of the Birr crawling toward 40 Br to a dollar: "The floating of the currency in such an import-dependent nation implies nothing but inflation."

a667.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) projection
a667.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) projection
a667.speech: Projects that the disparity between GDP and inflation will continue up until 2025, although the gap will narrow significantly from 2023 onward.

a667.speaker: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.name: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD)
a667.title: Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.speech: Denied the speculated plan to introduce a floated exchange rate regime: "There is no floating plan whatsoever."

a667.speaker: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD), macroeconomist
a667.name: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD)
a667.title: macroeconomist
a667.speech: "Gradual exchange rate liberalisation should be employed, moving toward a flexible exchange rate."

a667.speaker: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD), Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.name: Eyob Tekalegn (PhD)
a667.title: Ethiopian State Minister for Finance
a667.speech: "The government will decisively deal with the forex imbalances through a comprehensive set of measures." ; said mobilising forex, easing controls on forex sales to the private sector, allowing the exchange rate to become more flexible and market-determined, and implementing prudent fiscal and monetary policies are the measures planned by the government ; "The objective is to correct the real exchange rate overvaluation, steadily moving toward the alignment of the real exchange rate with economic fundamentals, and improve the competitiveness of our exports in the global markets."

a667.speaker: Macroeconomic pundits (unnamed)
a667.name: Macroeconomic pundits (unnamed)
a667.speech: Said that, short of a surgical approach to address the structural limitations in the economy, what the reform aspires to accomplish will have little to solve.

a667.speaker: Getachew T. Alemu, economist and consultant
a667.name: Getachew T. Alemu
a667.title: economist and consultant
a667.speech: Said the reform document may sound good in its diagnostic approach, but it does not have clear expected goals and targets: "This triggers a question; 'money for what?'" ; argued that Abiy's administration has been trying to correct the imbalance with a facilitative aspect of the economy, not the structural constraints: "The macro stance of the nation has not changed." ; "Nothing has come in the form of policy that improves exports, enhances import substitution, reduces logistics costs, stabilises the agricultural value chain and reprioritises public investments."

a667.speaker: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD), macroeconomist
a667.name: Eyob Tesfaye (PhD)
a667.title: macroeconomist
a667.speech: Said policymakers should start by adjusting some of the fiscal and monetary policies that will enable them to correct macroeconomic imbalances: "They have to go back to the drawing board and redefine their monetary policy stance." ; recommended arresting and containing inflation, introducing an indirect monetary policy stance, introducing a government borrowing limit and liberalising interest rates, plus moving toward a balanced budget, ceasing capital investments without feasibility studies, restructuring and recapitalising government banks, fundamental reforms for the commercial and development banks, and introducing a mortgage bank ; said the government should expect a maximum GDP growth of seven to eight percent, and advised that sequencing, timing and speed are crucial to the reform: "There has to be strong supervision from the Prime Minister himself." ; "There should be no room for failure."

a683.speaker: Event organisers (eHealth Africa, PSI, Population Council and Reach Digital Health) - statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES
a683.name: Event organisers (eHealth Africa
a683.title: PSI, Population Council and Reach Digital Health) - statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES
a683.speech: Said the dialogue themed "African-led Innovation: Shaping Sustainable Futures With or Without Aid" will explore how African countries can chart development paths independent of shrinking donor support ; noted the side event will amplify Africa's ingenuity and leadership in charting a new development path ; "In 2025, donor funding has faced unprecedented cuts, with a 17 per cent decline in Official Development Assistance and the near-total withdrawal of the United States from its role as the world's largest aid contributor" ; added that the event builds on the momentum of the Insights Learning Forum (ILF) 2025, where stakeholders called for harmonised digital health strategies, locally driven investment, and stronger domestic resource mobilisation.

a683.speaker: eHealth Africa (organisation)
a683.name: eHealth Africa (organisation)
a683.speech: Said the dialogue comes against the backdrop of declining donor funding, rising global inequalities, and the urgent need for Africa to lead in designing and implementing digital innovations for sustainability, whether or not foreign aid is available.

a683.speaker: Stakeholders at the Insights Learning Forum (ILF) 2025
a683.name: Stakeholders at the Insights Learning Forum (ILF) 2025
a683.speech: Called for harmonised digital health strategies, locally driven investment, and stronger domestic resource mobilisation.

a683.speaker: Atef Fawaz, Executive Director of eHealth Africa
a683.name: Atef Fawaz
a683.title: Executive Director of eHealth Africa
a683.speech: Described the dialogue as an urgent call to action and emphasised the need for Africa to continue demonstrating resilience, sovereignty, and creativity across sectors for a sustainable future: "This is beyond just conversation. It's an urgent call to action-a challenge to stakeholders across sectors to take bold steps to deepen collaboration, pool resources, and adopt adaptive strategies to sustain impact." ; "This is why we are bringing together industry leaders and think tanks to call for stronger partnerships that put African innovation at the centre of sustainable development."

a683.speaker: Michael Holscher, President of Population Services International (PSI)
a683.name: Michael Holscher
a683.title: President of Population Services International (PSI)
a683.speech: Noted that African innovation is transforming health delivery across the continent and beyond; said the most powerful solutions are coming from people with lived experience and led by experts who are building systems designed for true health sovereignty; said PSI is honoured to stand with its partners driving this unstoppable momentum of African ingenuity, advancing progress with or without external aid.

a683.speaker: Debbie Rogers, CEO of Reach Digital Health
a683.name: Debbie Rogers
a683.title: CEO of Reach Digital Health
a683.speech: Highlighted the growing impact of user-centred approaches on the continent; said Africa-led user-centric solutions are delivering measurable gains across the continent, from frontline services to national platforms, and that to accelerate this progress there is need for deeper collaboration and sustained investment.

a683.speaker: eHealth Africa and its partners (conveners)
a683.name: eHealth Africa and its partners (conveners)
a683.speech: Urged stakeholders across civil society organisations, private sector innovators, academia and governments to support and fund African-led initiatives while ensuring that health and development solutions remain nationally owned and community-driven.

a690.speaker: NBC News
a690.name: NBC News
a690.speech: According to NBC News, the termination of the committee was confirmed in a letter sent to members after a virtual meeting last Friday.

a690.speaker: CDC letter to HICPAC members
a690.name: CDC letter to HICPAC members
a690.speech: According to the CDC letter, HICPAC has made 540 recommendations to the agency since its inception, more than three decades ago, 90 per cent of which were fully implemented.

a690.speaker: Experts who spoke with NBC News
a690.name: Experts who spoke with NBC News
a690.speech: Raised concerns that the termination of the committee will leave healthcare facilities without essential tools to address emerging threats, such as drug-resistant bacteria and new infectious diseases.

a690.speaker: Connie Steed, HICPAC member since 2023 and former president of the Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology
a690.name: Connie Steed
a690.title: HICPAC member since 2023 and former president of the Association for Professionals in Infection Control and Epidemiology
a690.speech: "At some point, when things need to change, the guidelines likely won't change, and then people will be sort of flying by the seat of their pants."

a690.speaker: Anurag Malani, fellow at the Infectious Diseases Society of America who joined HICPAC in January
a690.name: Anurag Malani
a690.title: fellow at the Infectious Diseases Society of America who joined HICPAC in January
a690.speech: Said the committee was close to finalising new guidelines for airborne pathogens before the termination.

a690.speaker: NBC News
a690.name: NBC News
a690.speech: Reports that the guidelines, which had not been updated since 2007, included a controversial recommendation that would allow surgical masks instead of N95 respirators to prevent the spread of certain pathogens.

a690.speaker: Jane Thomason, lead hygienist at National Nurses United
a690.name: Jane Thomason
a690.title: lead hygienist at National Nurses United
a690.speech: Also criticised the decision; stated that without HICPAC's public meetings, there is no longer any public access to the process for drafting CDC infection control guidance ; "This further undermines safety for patients, nurses, and other health care workers."

a690.speaker: CDC and the Department of Health and Human Services
a690.name: CDC and the Department of Health and Human Services
a690.speech: Did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News.

a871.speaker: Mr Bako, Ministry of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity of Burkina Faso
a871.name: Mr Bako
a871.title: Ministry of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity of Burkina Faso
a871.speech: Presented the “Prevention mechanism in humanitarian action: the case of the Ministry of Humanitarian Action and National Solidarity” and recalled the fundamental role of his institution: “To coordinate, implement and evaluate humanitarian actions, ensuring their conformity with humanitarian principles and the needs of vulnerable populations. The ministry also works to reduce vulnerability, strengthen community capacities and protect the rights of people affected by crises.”

a871.speaker: Me Prospère Farama, REN-LAC
a871.name: Me Prospère Farama
a871.title: REN-LAC
a871.speech: Shared the lessons drawn from the “Tiegnan trial,” a case in which he played a decisive role, in a presentation entitled “The Tiegnan affair: what lessons for strengthening the fight against corruption in humanitarian action?”; for him the trial highlights three essential aspects: “First, the forms of corruption; then the question of the effectiveness of the prevention and repression mechanisms put in place by the public authorities, and also of the effectiveness of judicial repression in the fight against corruption; and finally, this trial challenged us on certain questions, namely the place of sociological and cultural constraints in our fight against corruption.”

a1010.speaker: Some component source countries
a1010.name: Some component source countries
a1010.speech: Had made it clear that they had no interest in manufacturing within the African continent.

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, Chief Executive Officer of the Botswana Institute for Technology Research and Innovation (BITRI)
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Botswana Institute for Technology Research and Innovation (BITRI)
a1010.speech: In an interview with the Botswana Guardian, shared that the next significant step is to begin production using the ordered components for the SUVs and buses, which will then be launched into the market: "It's important to note that as part of the agreement, we need to start with 50 SUVs and 30 buses" ; "We've already made payments for those components, and they are en route to Botswana, including components for the 30 buses" ; He also noted that shipping components from China to Botswana takes around six weeks, though unexpected delays beyond anyone's control could extend that timeframe: "But if the parts arrive in eight weeks, we should be able to assemble them."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: Revealed that BITRI has trained a total of 150 technicians, and added that they work with panel beaters, auto-mechanics, electricians and welders who had either done certificate or diploma: "The training of technicians continues because we need a total of 300, but unfortunately, we will not be able to absorb them, but all the companies around will absorb them as they are bringing in the EVs."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: Responding to criticism that BITRI is merely assembling rather than manufacturing the vehicles, clarified: "What we often overlook as a country is that all vehicles, regardless of the maker, are assembled. Major car manufacturers operate within an ecosystem where different components are produced separately and later brought together at an assembly line. Here in Botswana, while we may initially source components from a supplier, the vehicles will be assembled locally."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: Asked about the steps Botswana has taken to avoid repeating the failure of the Hyundai plant, explained that industrial espionage makes it hard to predict competitors' actions, adding: "As part of our agreements with the companies, anyone wanting to purchase this particular model will have to come to Botswana. We are confident that we have safeguarded our interests."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: Said that parallel to assembling they had to consider the infrastructure associated with e-mobility including charging stations, especially fast chargers: "Each of these vehicles is fitted with its own standard charger that can be plugged in your house and charge the entire night as they are slow if you are starting from scratch." ; He explained that they did a study of where the infrastructure will be established within the country so that they can easily be accessible: "We have also looked at the fact that if they could be plugged in the grid, they will put in a lot of burden on the BPC grid hence we looked in the places of having them off grid. We have even investigated not having them as solar-charged but also as hydrogen fuel sellers technology. We have a partner in Israel who had developed hydrogen fuel to the point where it is 90 - 95 percent cheaper."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: Explained that the project was initially housed within the government enclave, that the Ministry attempted to manage it internally but due to underlying challenges it didn't work out, and that eventually the President decided the project needed to be moved to an agency capable of implementing it ; On the project phases: "However, we soon realised that reaching the prototype stage for the electric vehicle would take much longer than expected. So, we redefined the design concept, shifting from 'electric vehicle' to 'e-mobility,' which opened the door for a broader range of electric transport solutions, including motorbikes, boats, or other types of vehicles." ; He added that as part of this approach they partnered with Aliboats in Maun: "We brought in international partners to assist with the design, and the boat was developed swiftly. There were some issues during testing, primarily related to the boat's weight and the need to adjust the motors. But a year ago, after testing in Kasane, the boat was finalised, since there was no water in Maun."

a1010.speaker: Professor Shedden Masupe, BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.name: Professor Shedden Masupe
a1010.title: BITRI Chief Executive Officer
a1010.speech: "Eventually, we received a strong proposal from a Zimbabwean company that addressed all our requirements, especially regarding technology transfer. However, during final negotiations, we discovered they didn't possess the intellectual property (IP) or the authorisation to assemble vehicles - they were simply reselling vehicles they had in Zimbabwe." ; He highlighted that Botswana's Ambassador in China, Dr Batlang Serema, helped BITRI by connecting them with several companies in the e-mobility sector, as China is a global leader in this field ; He said recently Chinese experts arrived to train BITRI's technicians, who had previously undergone training in electric vehicle assembly using smaller electric vehicles at BITRI centres in Francistown and Kanye.

a1010.speaker: Skywell and CHTC (Chinese vehicle manufacturers)
a1010.name: Skywell and CHTC (Chinese vehicle manufacturers)
a1010.speech: Expressed interest in partnering with BITRI; the Chinese companies promised to support BITRI in setting up operations, and stood out for their willingness to transfer their IP, to negotiate terms for sharing any new IP developed jointly in the future, and to source components from local manufacturers in Botswana.

a1054.speaker: Rachael Nsubuga, Senior Trade Facilitation Officer at the African Development Bank
a1054.name: Rachael Nsubuga
a1054.title: Senior Trade Facilitation Officer at the African Development Bank
a1054.speech: Said the bank's trade facilitation programs are designed to reduce barriers to international trade and facilitate both intra-African and external trade: "This project will complement other programs of the African Development Bank in the region by providing digitalized trade solutions and data to support investment climate and customs modernization work."

a1054.speaker: Dr. Peter Matuki, Secretary General of the East African Community Secretariat
a1054.name: Dr. Peter Matuki
a1054.title: Secretary General of the East African Community Secretariat
a1054.speech: "The EAC is committed to trade transparency and partnerships in developing regional trade. Enabling infrastructure coupled with capacity building can further bolster the region's trade ecosystem for sustained socio-economic gains."

a1259.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a1259.name: Donald Trump
a1259.title: US President-elect
a1259.speech: Asked senators on Sunday to exempt him from their approval, in principle mandatory, to appoint the highest officials of his future administration. ; "Sometimes the votes can take two years or more. That's what they (the Democrats) did four years ago and we cannot let that happen again," the president-elect protested on X on Sunday, referring to his first term (2017-2021). ; "Any Republican senator seeking the coveted position of leader in the US Senate must accept appointments" made outside parliamentary sessions, he added.

a1259.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a1259.name: Donald Trump
a1259.title: US President-elect
a1259.speech: "No judge should be approved" before the Republicans have chosen their leader and taken office in the Senate, Donald Trump added on Sunday.

a1259.speaker: Rick Scott, US Senator elected in Florida
a1259.name: Rick Scott
a1259.title: US Senator elected in Florida
a1259.speech: "100% agree. I will do anything to get your appointments (approved) as quickly as possible," wrote Rick Scott.

a1259.speaker: John Thune, US Senator for South Dakota, number two Republican in the Senate
a1259.name: John Thune
a1259.title: US Senator for South Dakota, number two Republican in the Senate
a1259.speech: "We must act quickly and decisively so that the people appointed by the president are approved and all options are on the table, including that of appointment during a parliamentary recess," declared John Thune.

a1259.speaker: John Cornyn, US Senator for Texas
a1259.name: John Cornyn
a1259.title: US Senator for Texas
a1259.speech: "It is unacceptable that Democratic senators are blocking" the appointments, declared John Cornyn. "If they do, we will stay in session even on weekends until they give in. And the Constitution gives the president the power to make appointments during recesses," he added.

a1334.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) Executive Board, first regular session of 2024 (decision/recommendations)
a1334.name: World Food Programme (WFP) Executive Board
a1334.title: first regular session of 2024 (decision/recommendations)
a1334.speech: Recommended that WFP increase the support provided to the least developed countries in the fight against vulnerability, poverty, food insecurity, malnutrition and inequality, and that it support social protection programmes in rural and urban areas and the redistribution of resources that help people meet their essential needs. Under the decision, WFP will pay particular attention to the implementation of the Doha Programme of Action for the Least Developed Countries, within the framework of the support it provides to them and in accordance with its mandate.

a1334.speaker: Youssef Balla, President of the WFP Executive Board (and other board members)
a1334.name: Youssef Balla
a1334.title: President of the WFP Executive Board (and other board members)
a1334.speech: Stress that the UN institution will rely on its 2022-2025 Strategic Plan and its normative framework, which are consistent with the Doha Programme of Action and its priority areas of action.

a1334.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) Executive Board decision
a1334.name: World Food Programme (WFP) Executive Board decision
a1334.speech: States that the opportunities offered by global and local partnerships will be explored, drawing for example on UNICEF's specialised expertise on matters concerning children, families and essential services, and on that of the World Bank in reforming social protection systems and developing policies.

a1483.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1483.name: Donald Trump
a1483.title: US President
a1483.speech: Praised Africa’s exceptional economic potential and called for building win-win partnerships based on trade and investment rather than aid.

a1483.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1483.name: Donald Trump
a1483.title: US President
a1483.speech: Emphasized the need for peace as a prerequisite for any development, announcing an expanded U.S.-Africa summit in the fall to deepen these discussions.

a1499.speaker: Dangote Group (statement signed by Anthony Chiejina, Group Chief Branding & Communications Officer)
a1499.name: Dangote Group (statement signed by Anthony Chiejina
a1499.title: Group Chief Branding & Communications Officer)
a1499.speech: confirmed the retirement of foremost entrepreneur and founder of Dangote Cement Plc, Aliko Dangote, as a Director and the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement, effective July 25. A statement signed by Anthony Chiejina said Mr Dangote is relinquishing his position as chairman and retiring from the board so as to focus more attention on the refinery, petrochemicals, fertiliser and government relations, in order to drive the company's five-year business trajectory to a superlative height. The company also confirmed the appointment of Emmanuel Ikazoboh, an independent non-executive director, as the new Chairman, Board of Directors. "In the same vein, Hajiya Mariya Aliko Dangote was also appointed to the Board of Directors of the Company while Prof. Dorothy Ufot retired from the Board," it said.

a1499.speaker: Aliko Dangote, founder of Dangote Cement Plc
a1499.name: Aliko Dangote
a1499.title: founder of Dangote Cement Plc
a1499.speech: has announced his retirement as a Director and the Chairman of the Board of Directors, effective July 25, 2025. He is relinquishing his position as chairman and retiring from the board so as to focus more attention on the Refinery, Petrochemicals, Fertiliser and Government Relations, in order to drive the company's five-year business trajectory to a superlative height.

a1499.speaker: Dangote Cement Plc unaudited results for the six months ending 30 June 2025 (company report)
a1499.name: Dangote Cement Plc unaudited results for the six months ending 30 June 2025 (company report)
a1499.speech: According to the unaudited results, the group revenue went up by 17.7 percent, from N1,760 billion at the same period in 2024 to N2,071.6 billion, representing the highest revenue in the history of the company. Group EBITDA grew by 41.8 percent to N944.900 billion from N666.22 billion; EBITDA (Nigeria Operations) grew by 82.4 percent to N845.4 billion; profit before tax went up from N292.96 billion to N730 billion; profit after tax surged by 174.1 percent to N520.5 billion. Export volumes from Nigeria increased by 18.2 percent, with 18 successful clinker shipments made to Ghana and Cameroon.

a1499.speaker: Emmanuel Ikazoboh, new Chairman of the Board of Dangote Cement Plc (acceptance speech)
a1499.name: Emmanuel Ikazoboh
a1499.title: new Chairman of the Board of Dangote Cement Plc (acceptance speech)
a1499.speech: said he is truly honored to accept the role of Chairman of Dangote Cement Plc while pledging to uphold the highest standards of leadership and dedication in this role. He described the company as a beacon of African enterprise, which has consistently demonstrated resilience, innovation, and a commitment to excellence. ; "my vision for Dangote Cement Plc is built upon a foundation of sustainable growth, operational efficiency, and unwavering commitment to our core values. We will continue to focus on the following key priorities, Operational Excellence, Strategic Expansion, Sustainability, Innovation and Community Engagement." ; He stated the company will accelerate efforts to adopt alternative fuels and technologies, reducing reliance on fossil fuels, and promised that the company will continue to invest in training and development, fostering a culture of excellence and empowering employees to reach their full potential.

a1638.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1638.name: Daniel Chapo
a1638.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1638.speech: Demands accountability for all individuals involved in financial crimes in the Public Administration. Daniel Chapo wants greater strategic coordination and information sharing between the Administrative Court and the bodies of justice administration and investigation, in order to eliminate barriers in the fight against fraud and corruption.

a1638.speaker: Emilia Moiane, Director of the Information Office (Gabinete de Informacao)
a1638.name: Emilia Moiane
a1638.title: Director of the Information Office (Gabinete de Informacao)
a1638.speech: Said AIM, the Mozambican news agency, must position itself in the mission of promoting the country's achievements, the consolidation of national unity, national interests, and the promotion of democracy and social justice. These were the words of the director of the information office, speaking at the swearing-in ceremony on Wednesday in Maputo of Orlando Gambeta, the new director general of AIM.

a1638.speaker: Banana producers in Gorongosa
a1638.name: Banana producers in Gorongosa
a1638.speech: Call for the harmonisation of the selling price of bananas. They want bananas to be sold by the kilogram and not by the bunch.

a1700.speaker: Participants of the first Annual International Forum on the Development of Liptako-Gourma (FIA)
a1700.name: Participants of the first Annual International Forum on the Development of Liptako-Gourma (FIA)
a1700.speech: After three days of discussions and sharing of experience, the participants formulated a number of recommendations, including the strengthening of cooperation between member states in the face of complex challenges, the adoption of an inclusive approach with greater involvement of local communities in decision-making and in the implementation of development projects, the strengthening of the protection of populations, and increased investment in the empowerment of the region's young people and women; the forum also expressed the wish that funding from development partners be provided in a more flexible and multi-year manner in order to improve humanitarian aid and sustainable development actions.

a1700.speaker: Ismaël Wagué, Malian Minister of Reconciliation, Peace and National Cohesion (Army Corps General)
a1700.name: Ismaël Wagué
a1700.title: Malian Minister of Reconciliation, Peace and National Cohesion (Army Corps General)
a1700.speech: Welcomed the smooth running of the proceedings and called for the immediate implementation of the roadmap resulting from the forum; gave assurances that this forum would not be just one more forum but that it would be useful, to the great benefit of the people of the region.

a1700.speaker: Hawa Aw, Executive Secretary of the Liptako-Gourma Authority (ALG)
a1700.name: Hawa Aw
a1700.title: Executive Secretary of the Liptako-Gourma Authority (ALG)
a1700.speech: Thanked the Minister of Reconciliation for his involvement and support, which, according to her, contributed to the success of the forum; joined the minister in calling for a rapid realisation of the recommendations.

a1814.speaker: Government of Eswatini
a1814.name: Government of Eswatini
a1814.speech: Terms the receipt of five immigrants from the US as following 'rigorous negotiations and due diligence'; Hospital Hill tweeted 'welcome' through a press statement meant to allay the nation's fears.

a1814.speaker: Washington (US government, via tweets)
a1814.name: Washington (US government
a1814.title: via tweets)
a1814.speech: All we got while analysing tweets coming out of Washington was 'adios'.

a1814.speaker: Adam Smith, father of economics
a1814.name: Adam Smith
a1814.title: father of economics
a1814.speech: "It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker, that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves, not to their humanity but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our own necessities but of their advantages."

a2131.speaker: Former Ministry of Agriculture official (anonymous), industry insider
a2131.name: Former Ministry of Agriculture official (anonymous)
a2131.title: industry insider
a2131.speech: Claimed the scheme benefits a select group of influential individuals: "These people rake in millions every day, while farmers are left struggling," the official said, requesting anonymity.

a2131.speaker: Nyambene Miraa Trade Association (Nyamita)
a2131.name: Nyambene Miraa Trade Association (Nyamita)
a2131.speech: In 2022 sounded the alarm about these levies, describing how exporters were coerced into paying a "commission" at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA), and that airlines were allegedly directed to assist in collecting the fees.

a2131.speaker: Kathuri Murungi, Meru Senator
a2131.name: Kathuri Murungi
a2131.title: Meru Senator
a2131.speech: Acknowledged the Ministry of Trade's awareness of the levy but criticized its failure to act decisively. "Even efforts by the Kenyan Ambassador to Somalia have failed to dismantle this deeply entrenched cartel," he lamented.

a2131.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a2131.name: William Ruto
a2131.title: President of Kenya
a2131.speech: Pledged during his 2022 campaign to eliminate the cartel.

a2131.speaker: Kimathi Munjuri, Nyamita spokesperson
a2131.name: Kimathi Munjuri
a2131.title: Nyamita spokesperson
a2131.speech: Highlights how the so-called "commission" has distorted the miraa market in Somalia, making the commodity less affordable.

a2286.speaker: Ryad Mezzour, Morocco's Minister of Industry
a2286.name: Ryad Mezzour
a2286.title: Morocco's Minister of Industry
a2286.speech: Stressed that in less than two decades the Moroccan aeronautics sector has become a world-class aeronautics industry, with export turnover rising from less than one billion dirhams in 2004 to more than 26 billion in 2024. With an ecosystem bringing together more than 150 international players present on its territory, the Kingdom has built a high-performing aeronautics industry. He hailed the royal vision that has enabled Morocco to become an essential destination in this cutting-edge sector.

a2286.speaker: Ross McInnes, Chairman of the Safran group
a2286.name: Ross McInnes
a2286.title: Chairman of the Safran group
a2286.speech: Hailed the Kingdom's exemplary investment environment, stating that Safran "does not produce in Morocco, but with Morocco".

a2286.speaker: Olivier Andries, Chief Executive Officer of Safran
a2286.name: Olivier Andries
a2286.title: Chief Executive Officer of Safran
a2286.speech: Stressed that the choice of Morocco is based on its talent, its modern infrastructure and its macroeconomic stability, adding that the projects under way represent more than 350 million euros of investment.

a2336.speaker: Ethiopian Bankers Association
a2336.name: Ethiopian Bankers Association
a2336.speech: On behalf of 18 commercial banks, has asked for an explanation on how to make the financial support, amounting to an estimated 400 million Br ; addressed to the Addis Abeba Mayor's Office, the Ministry of Defense, and the Amhara regional government, the Association wrote a letter seeking advice on sharing the donation between federal and regional governments and urging them to decide where the donation be deposited.

a2336.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a2336.name: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a2336.speech: Said the banks' contributions amount to an estimated 400 million Br and that insurance firms and microfinance institutions are expected to contribute up to 100 million Br.

a2336.speaker: Abie Sano, president of the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) and chairperson of the Ethiopian Bankers Association
a2336.name: Abie Sano
a2336.title: president of the Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE) and chairperson of the Ethiopian Bankers Association
a2336.speech: According to Abie, the Association has yet to make the contributions.

a2336.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2336.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a2336.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2336.speech: Told parliament last month that his administration had spent over 100 billion Br to pay for the war and humanitarian provisions in Tigray.

a2336.speaker: Ermias Andarge, president of Enat Bank
a2336.name: Ermias Andarge
a2336.title: president of Enat Bank
a2336.speech: "We've agreed to raise the contribution through the Association."

a2336.speaker: Gizachew Muluneh, communications affairs director of the Amhara regional government
a2336.name: Gizachew Muluneh
a2336.title: communications affairs director of the Amhara regional government
a2336.speech: Told Fortune that the Regional State requires an estimated four billion Birr to cover operational costs for the war against armed forces in Tigray and the surrounding areas, an amount that excludes the two billion Birr reimbursement the regional government is awaiting from the federal government for costs incurred in providing medical treatment to members of the national defence forces ; Gizachew did not disclose how much of the four billion Birr the regional state has mobilised.

a2336.speaker: Officials of the Addis Abeba City Administration
a2336.name: Officials of the Addis Abeba City Administration
a2336.speech: Were not available for comment despite repeated attempts.

a2448.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC), Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report for the week ending November 3)
a2448.name: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC)
a2448.title: Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report for the week ending November 3)
a2448.speech: Reported that Zimbabwe recorded 17 new cases of anthrax at the beginning of the month and that no human anthrax-related deaths were reported: “The cases were reported from Gokwe North district (14) and Gokwe South district (2) in Midlands province and Mutoko district (1) in Mashonaland East province. The cumulative figures for anthrax cases are 421 and 0 deaths.”

a2448.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC), Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.name: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC)
a2448.title: Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.speech: Said during the same week 25 new mumps cases were recorded although there were no fatalities, bringing the cumulative number of cases to 6 881 with no deaths.

a2448.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC), Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.name: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC)
a2448.title: Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.speech: Reported 7 529 common diarrhoea cases and one death during the week under review: “The death was reported from Sally Mugabe Central Hospital in Harare Metropolitan province. Of the reported cases, 3 138 (42%) were from under five years of age”; the provinces that reported the highest number of cases were Manicaland (1 232) and Mashonaland Central (1 208).

a2448.speaker: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC), Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.name: Ministry of Health and Child Care (MHCC)
a2448.title: Zimbabwe (disease surveillance report)
a2448.speech: Said there were no new confirmed Mpox cases in the country, whose cumulative figure stands at two with no fatalities ; “Eight suspected typhoid cases and no deaths were reported this week. The cumulative figure for suspected typhoid cases is 249 and 0 deaths.”

a2454.speaker: Kofi Annan, chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Kofi Annan
a2454.title: chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Speaking to the BBC ahead of the report launch, told the BBC that African people are “not getting the revenues we deserve”; suggested that at the heart of this issue is a lack of transparency around production-sharing agreements and the sale of assets to foreign investors.

a2454.speaker: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.name: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.speech: “No country better illustrates the high costs associated with opaque concession trading than the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)” ; “Privatization of the DRC's minerals sector has been plagued by a culture of secrecy, informal deals and allegations of corruption”; finds that the DRC lost at least $1.36 billion in revenues between 2010 and 2012 by underpricing mining assets sold to foreign companies, equivalent to $21 per citizen, with offshore companies' rate of return averaging 512% and as high as 980% in one deal.

a2454.speaker: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.name: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.speech: States it is not explicitly accusing political leaders, officials or the foreign companies involved of deliberately engaging in illegal activity, although it suggests investigation be carried out to determine whether the assets were “knowingly undervalued”, and notes that other huge losses in the sector have been incurred through a mixture of “poor management, corruption and flawed taxation policies”.

a2454.speaker: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.name: Africa Progress Panel (annual report)
a2454.speech: Lists causes for optimism, including an enormous opportunity to translate resources into improved outcomes for Africa's citizens because of the “commodity super-cycle”; but makes clear that many resource-rich countries are leaving the poor behind, with nine of the 12 countries at the very bottom of the Human Development Index rich in resources.

a2454.speaker: Kofi Annan, chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Kofi Annan
a2454.title: chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: “Tax avoidance and evasion are global issues that affect us all”; announced that the panel would be bringing a number of suggestions on taxation reform to the G8 summit next month, including a rule-based global system on tax transparency, a clamp-down on illicit flows by offshore finance hubs, adoption by all countries of measures equivalent to the Dodd Frank Act, and forcing foreign-owned companies to disclose the “ultimate beneficiaries of profit”.

a2454.speaker: Kofi Annan, chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Kofi Annan
a2454.title: chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Said they estimated that high commodity prices would remain for another decade: “This is good news” ; “Resource wealth can bring millions out of poverty. It is eminently possible…but it will take bold leadership.”

a2454.speaker: Kofi Annan, chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Kofi Annan
a2454.title: chair of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Was quick to stress that their recommendations and critiques applied as much to China as to any western country.

a2454.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, head of Oxfam International
a2454.name: Winnie Byanyima
a2454.title: head of Oxfam International
a2454.speech: At a WEF session the previous day, had warned against a “race to the bottom” when it comes to mineral rights, saying that African governments sacrificed too much while wooing investment.

a2454.speaker: Linah Mohohlo, governor of the Bank of Botswana
a2454.name: Linah Mohohlo
a2454.title: governor of the Bank of Botswana
a2454.speech: Said sternly that if tax concessions have to be given in order to attract business, all details must be made public and the duration of such breaks must be necessarily limited; maintained that partnerships between African states and extractive industry players have to be clearly defined ; asserted her belief that such a partnership should not lead to a less than 50-50 split between state and private companies in revenues derived from a country's natural resources, and, asked whether she was endorsing nationalization, replied “Not at all”, but felt it a point of basic fairness that “a country has to come out with a higher percentage of profits that will flow from natural resources”.

a2454.speaker: Strive Masiyiwa, telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Strive Masiyiwa
a2454.title: telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Said there was little doubt that the report amounted to “a bit of a reality check”, especially as the panel had met to discuss its findings against the “sobering” backdrop of Marikana ; “The idea is not to put a damper on our confidence, but to look at all the issues”; “Is there equity in growth?”

a2454.speaker: Strive Masiyiwa, telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Strive Masiyiwa
a2454.title: telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Pointed out that in Africa there are 30 million children who are not in school, and said the region's mineral wealth has to be converted to human capital, with greater public investment in health, education, and basic social safety nets; also suggested that the way business has traditionally viewed Africa needs to change, the extractive industry having tended to be afflicted by “short-termism”, and that incentives need to be created for long-term, high-quality investments.

a2454.speaker: Strive Masiyiwa, telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.name: Strive Masiyiwa
a2454.title: telecoms magnate and member of the Africa Progress Panel
a2454.speech: Asked by a journalist whether the growth figures could be a false dawn for Africa, replied: “If it's a false dawn, it's been going on for a while.”

a2454.speaker: Brooks Spector, Daily Maverick
a2454.name: Brooks Spector
a2454.title: Daily Maverick
a2454.speech: Pointed out on Thursday that the ‘C-word’ – China – has been strangely seldom heard at the WEF.

a2572.speaker: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.name: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.speech: According to the latest IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, the number of Basotho facing severe food insecurity has decreased by 68,000 people, from 403,000 in May 2024 to a projected 335,000 between January and March 2025; the report attributes the improvement to ongoing humanitarian assistance, including cash and food transfers from the government, humanitarian organisations, and United Nations (UN) agencies ; states that around 335,000 people – 22 percent of Lesotho’s rural population – are still expected to be in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) during the lean season from October 2024 to March 2025, with all ten districts remaining classified under this phase.

a2572.speaker: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.name: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.speech: Warns of several hazards that could exacerbate food insecurity: heavy rainfall, with forecasts predicting normal to above-normal precipitation, combined with high temperatures, could negatively impact agricultural output; and declining income sources, such as lower livestock sales due to market competition and restrictions on livestock movement to South Africa, further strain vulnerable households ; “Rising food, fuel, and electricity prices continue to erode purchasing power, making it harder for many families to afford basic necessities. Although food markets remain stable and functional, high costs are limiting accessibility for many Basotho.”

a2572.speaker: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.name: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.speech: Underscores the significant impact of humanitarian assistance: in Berea, 29 percent of the population received support, covering 67 percent of their caloric needs; “In Botha-Bothe and Leribe, assistance covered 72 percent and 65 percent of caloric needs, respectively, while in Qacha’s Nek, 27 percent of the population received aid, meeting 83 percent of their energy requirements.”

a2572.speaker: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.name: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis (report)
a2572.speech: Stated that food access remains a major concern, particularly for the most vulnerable districts, and calls for continued and expanded humanitarian aid to mitigate ongoing food insecurity; recommends scaling up anticipatory actions to address expected hazards and expanding both conditional and unconditional humanitarian assistance; urges the full implementation of the National Strategic Resilience Framework to help households diversify their livelihoods and withstand future shocks; other key recommendations include reducing food consumption gaps through subsidies and improved access to food, strengthening nutrition education, particularly on feeding practices and breastfeeding, and updating baseline profiles to enhance data availability for food security analysis.

a2572.speaker: Ntsokoane Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2572.name: Ntsokoane Matekane
a2572.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2572.speech: On July 12, 2024, declared a state of national food insecurity disaster following a historic drought, driven by El Niño, which resulted in the lowest crop yields since the 2018/19 agricultural season.

a2572.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a2572.name: Government of Lesotho
a2572.speech: Estimated that approximately 700,000 people – about a third of Lesotho’s population – would face hunger through March 2025, with over 400,000 in rural areas expected to experience crisis levels of acute hunger.

a2572.speaker: USAID
a2572.name: USAID
a2572.speech: Previously highlighted that climate shocks, diseases, and economic conditions would continue to drive high levels of acute food insecurity in Lesotho.

a2572.speaker: Experts
a2572.name: Experts
a2572.speech: Warn that sustained intervention is necessary to ensure long-term food security for Basotho.

a2653.speaker: Candide Azannai, member of the National Assembly of Benin, member of the presidential majority and president of the party “Restaurer l’espoir”
a2653.name: Candide Azannai
a2653.title: member of the National Assembly of Benin, member of the presidential majority and president of the party “Restaurer l’espoir”
a2653.speech: “The reforms undertaken at the Autonomous Port of Cotonou are noble. It is the pursuit of [private] interests that explains the disinformation surrounding the (PVI).” ; “The disinformation surrounding the PVI comes from those who wear masks and who, behind them, play with the interests of the people.” ; Affirmed his support for the implementation of the new-generation import verification programme (PVI), which according to him is one of the achievements of the “refoundation”, and believes the PVI is an indispensable development reform. For him, the head of State must stand firm and above all avoid being intimidated by the port mafia. He believes this programme is not an invention of the current regime; an attempt at implementation had been begun without success under the Kérékou regime, and since the State is a continuity, the work begun had to be completed. “The PVI is a computerised management of the entry of port revenues into the State’s coffers and it must be tested in order to perceive its long-term effects.” He is surprised that after two months of implementation this programme is a subject of discord and of disinformation coming from all sides. He also encourages President Boni Yayi in his patriotic drive and his determination to clean up the port platform. “The government must assert its authority and avoid letting itself be distracted. There are operators who appreciate the reform, but those who criticise it are the fraudsters who do not want things to move forward,” he stated.

a2653.speaker: Candide Azannai, member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.name: Candide Azannai
a2653.title: member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.speech: Asked about the magistrates’ strike, the MP deplores the lack of solidarity within the government. He believes there is a trivialisation of the authority of the State and that Minister Gbèdo found herself alone facing the magistrates, who nevertheless are not free of all suspicion of being corrupt men. He states that corruption is a societal phenomenon that spares no one and that doctrine in fact prohibits strikes by magistrates in the judicial sector.

a2653.speaker: Candide Azannai, member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.name: Candide Azannai
a2653.title: member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.speech: As for the teachers’ strike, the speaker believes that they must take into account the State’s limited resources and moderate their demands.

a2653.speaker: Candide Azannai, member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.name: Candide Azannai
a2653.title: member of the National Assembly of Benin
a2653.speech: On the management of the National Assembly, he believes that President Nago does not have a command of the texts and takes anti-democratic initiatives. To illustrate this, he mentioned the plan for a parliamentary retirement scheme at the president’s initiative — an act which, according to him, is at odds with the spirit of parliament.

a2743.speaker: Reza Salehi Amiri, Iranian Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts
a2743.name: Reza Salehi Amiri
a2743.title: Iranian Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts
a2743.speech: Said Iran is intensifying its efforts to protect and promote its cultural heritage and tourism sector to achieve top-tier recognition from UNESCO ; articulated a vision for the future, revealing that Iran is developing comprehensive five-year and twenty-year plans dedicated to elevating its tourism industry.

a2743.speaker: Iran Press News Agency (partner of TV BRICS)
a2743.name: Iran Press News Agency (partner of TV BRICS)
a2743.speech: Reported that under the seventh development plan Iran is targeting a significant increase in health tourism, aiming to attract 2 million medical tourists and generate a projected revenue of US$6 billion, up from the current US$1.2 billion, and that Iran will be investing heavily in infrastructural development, promotional campaigns and international collaborations.

a2747.speaker: Said Nour, Director General of CRIPEN; Ayane Osman, Executive Secretary for General Education; and Moussa Hassan, USAID-Djibouti project officer
a2747.name: Said Nour
a2747.title: Director General of CRIPEN; Ayane Osman, Executive Secretary for General Education; and Moussa Hassan, USAID-Djibouti project officer
a2747.speech: All took part in the closing ceremony of the workshop and respectively recalled the importance of this workshop for MENFOP's curriculum writers.

a2900.speaker: Michael Gonzales, United States of America Ambassador to Zambia
a2900.name: Michael Gonzales
a2900.title: United States of America Ambassador to Zambia
a2900.speech: Has described Zambia's Sixth President Edgar Lungu, who died in South Africa last week, as a true leader with a clear vision for a strong and prosperous Zambia; Mr Gonzales has joined local and international dignitaries in mourning the death of President Lungu.

a2927.speaker: Standard Bank April PMI report
a2927.name: Standard Bank April PMI report
a2927.speech: “Growth was underpinned by an increase in sales, which helped to lift output and support a fresh rise in employment. Demand for inputs also led to the quickest increases in purchasing and inventories for nearly three years” ; supply chains “registered a further recovery, whilst cost inflation remained relatively mild. As a result, businesses were more confident that activity growth will continue, with sentiment rising to its highest level since May 2024” ; “The PMI rose from 50.2 in March to 50.5 in April, posting above the 50.0 neutral mark for the third successive month” ; “The latest reading signalled a marginal uplift in operating conditions across the private sector in Mozambique” ; total output levels “rose for the third month running in April, albeit with the pace of expansion easing to the softest in this period” ; “New clients and rising sales were often associated with the upturn, as well as improved efficiency and efforts to increase the quality of products and services. A rise in demand encouraged firms to hire more staff” ; “Although the uplift in employment was the fastest seen in eight months, it was marginal and only partly offset a moderate reduction in March” ; expectations for future output “likewise strengthened in April”, with 42% of the companies surveyed admitting that they expect “activity to rise over the year ahead, pushing the overall degree of optimism to an 11-month high” ; “Higher sales and product development were often highlighted as supporting forecasts. Another factor helping lift confidence was a gradual recovery of supply chains, following disruption in late-2024 and early this year amid post-election protests.”

a2927.speaker: Fáusio Mussá, Standard Bank chief economist
a2927.name: Fáusio Mussá
a2927.title: Standard Bank chief economist
a2927.speech: Noted that “for the first time since June 2024, all PMI sub-indices came in at the level of 50 or above”, which denotes “month-on month expansions in economic activity in March and implying that the private sector is still in recovery from the negative impact of the protests that followed the October 2024 election.”

a2927.speaker: Fáusio Mussá, Standard Bank chief economist
a2927.name: Fáusio Mussá
a2927.title: Standard Bank chief economist
a2927.speech: “However, improved sentiment contrasts with increased global uncertainty and negative domestic developments, manifest in the IMF 3-year programme being suspended in April and the US cutting development assistance. This implies additional fiscal and foreign exchange liquidity pressures.”

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ) and former secretary-general of the Pan-African Youth Union, expert in peace and security, governance and elections
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ) and former secretary-general of the Pan-African Youth Union, expert in peace and security, governance and elections
a2971.speech: Declared at the 2nd Political Conference for the Autonomy of the Sahara in Dakhla on 29 April 2025 that the Sahel region is currently confronted with enormous multidimensional socio-economic challenges: “6.3 million people are displaced, 37.7 million people need urgent humanitarian aid and 21.8 million are in a situation of severe food insecurity. These challenges are amplified by the deterioration of the security situation due to the worsening terrorist threat and the resurgence of non-state armed and separatist groups, the impact of climate change and desertification”; he noted that between January and September 2023, West Africa recorded 1,027 attacks which caused 6,225 victims, and that the number of terrorism victims in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger rose from 800 in 2016 to nearly 10,000 victims in 2022.

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.speech: Said acts of interference in the internal affairs of Sahel countries and the sponsoring of international terrorism have not made the fight against these challenges easier; that his country decided to end the 2015 Algiers Accord on 27 March 2024 because of Algeria’s unfriendly acts and its interference in Mali’s internal affairs; that the Algerian president welcomes with open arms several Malian opponents and politicians “whom we consider separatists and terrorists”; that Algeria is misusing its current non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council for slanderous declarations against Mali when it could pay more attention to the question of self-determination of the Kabyle population; that a drone of Mali’s Armed and Security Forces was destroyed by a hostile act of the Algerian regime on the night of 31 March 2025 in the Kidal region, “an ignoble act [which] showed the true face of Algeria as a Godfather of international terrorism in the Sahel”; and that by this bellicose act Algeria supports international terrorism by obstructing Malian operations against armed, terrorist and separatist groups.

a2971.speaker: Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, Prime Minister of Mali (then Minister of State, Minister of Territorial Administration)
a2971.name: Major General Abdoulaye Maïga
a2971.title: Prime Minister of Mali (then Minister of State, Minister of Territorial Administration)
a2971.speech: Denounced the “paternalistic domination that Algeria sought to give itself over my country” and “an erroneous perception by the Algerian authorities who consider Mali as their backyard or a doormat State, against a backdrop of contempt and condescension” ; During the General Debate of the 79th session of the UN General Assembly last September, General Maïga reiterated Algeria’s serious interference in Mali’s internal affairs, hammering that “Mali will not stand idly by in the face of any attempt to undermine its sovereignty.”

a2971.speaker: College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES — Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso)
a2971.name: College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES — Mali
a2971.title: Niger and Burkina Faso)
a2971.speech: Announced several actions in response to this unfriendly act, including the immediate recall of their respective ambassadors in Algeria, the summoning of the Algerian ambassador to protest against the hostility of the Algerian regime, Mali’s withdrawal from the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee (Cémoc), as well as filing a complaint before international bodies against the Algerian regime for acts of aggression.

a2971.speaker: Government of Mali
a2971.name: Government of Mali
a2971.speech: Denounced this act of aggression by addressing a letter of protest against the Algerian regime to the members of the UN Security Council.

a2971.speaker: Algerian regime (communiqué)
a2971.name: Algerian regime (communiqué)
a2971.speech: To try to mask its ignoble act, the Algerian regime attempted a diversion in a fallacious communiqué in which it tries to say that the Malian authorities are no longer in step with the Malian people.

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.speech: Said “Morocco is the partner on which Mali can count”, citing as proof that during its presidency of the African Union Peace and Security Council last March the Kingdom added an agenda item for informal consultations with Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Gabon, Guinea and Sudan, currently suspended by the AU, to explore avenues for their full reintegration into the pan-African organisation; that the Sahel should not be reduced to a purely security dimension, as the region has enormous potential in renewable energy and hosts some of the largest aquifers on the African continent; and invited participants to join the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) in a win-win partnership.

a2971.speaker: His Majesty King Mohammed VI of Morocco (Royal Speech of 6 November 2023, 48th anniversary of the Green March)
a2971.name: His Majesty King Mohammed VI of Morocco (Royal Speech of 6 November 2023
a2971.title: 48th anniversary of the Green March)
a2971.speech: Underlined that to resolve the difficulties and problems facing the brotherly States of the Sahel, the solution cannot be exclusively security-based or military, but must be founded on an approach of cooperation and joint development, so as to favour the access of Sahel States to the Atlantic Ocean.

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: former president of Mali’s National Youth Council (CNJ)
a2971.speech: Said the international community must cease responding to the blackmail measures undertaken by Algiers; that “it is time to put an end to all this staging by Algeria aimed at taking Africa hostage through an entity in which no one believes”; and that Algeria is no longer able to block the settlement at the UN of this regional dispute, in the light of the clear positions of many countries in the world, “in particular the United States, which urge all parties to seal this file on the sole basis of the Moroccan Autonomy initiative” ; Concluded: “Long live Mali; Long live the AES; Long live Morocco; Long live the Sahel in a united and prosperous Africa.”

a2971.speaker: United States
a2971.name: United States
a2971.speech: Urge all parties to seal this file on the sole basis of the Moroccan Autonomy initiative (as cited by Souleymane Satigui Sidibé).

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.speech: Said that in global geopolitics, local governance has an important place in regional and sub-regional integration, because most disputes between States are political, not between peoples; “Dakhla is a textbook case. Given the transformation of this city, given the integration, the resettlement of African migrants who wanted to pass through there to go to Europe and who finally decided to settle in this region, it proves sufficiently that the policy of His Majesty King Mohammed VI in local governance, by strengthening local elected officials, is an important and better approach for regional integration.”

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
