a2971.title: expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.speech: Said cross-border security, violent extremism and trafficking in arms, drugs and human beings are activities carried out by terrorist groups, “forces of evil” that exploit the vulnerability of populations, mostly young people and vulnerable women; “For me, the regional cooperation approach to confront these harmful activities necessarily goes through development”; that in asymmetric warfare the civilian matters more than men in uniform; that Dakhla is a textbook case because the city is under full reconstruction, including businesses, restaurants and industries that create mass employment and dissuade young people and women from being recruited by terrorist groups; and that the royal decision to help Sahel countries gain access to the Atlantic Ocean is an important step in regional collaboration against cross-border insecurity, denoting Morocco’s serious and sincere partnership with these countries through “structured, sovereign and secure” opening-up.

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.speech: Said mechanisms of inclusive governance pass first through sincere collaboration between States, the involvement of grassroots communities in governance, and the willingness to let communities manage their own public affairs; that Morocco’s textbook case of proposing autonomy in the Moroccan Sahara is an example many countries could develop by strengthening what some call advanced regionalisation and others advanced decentralisation; and cited the hundreds of imams trained in Morocco and hundreds of thousands of African students educated there as references that allow Africans to be elites at the global level.

a2971.speaker: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé, expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.name: Souleymane Satigui Sidibé
a2971.title: expert in peace and security, governance and elections (interview with Medi 1)
a2971.speech: Said the support of the United States, Spain and Germany for Morocco’s autonomy proposal is “more an awakening of consciousness” to the realities of the Moroccan Sahara today and to the question of international security, because these great powers know that those who maintain separatist and terrorist groups do so in their own interest and to the detriment of international security; that this dynamic should encourage the United Nations to settle this question definitively; and that “Mali was obliged to expel the United Nations from Malian territory because after ten years, if we think that the world organisation that guarantees peace must maintain insecurity, it no longer has any reason to exist”, calling on the UN to abandon a role of impartiality that favours insecurity and the trafficking of humans and drugs in the Sahel.

a3076.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a3076.name: Government of Mozambique
a3076.speech: Has reaffirmed the modernisation of the Armed Forces as a national priority, underlining the urgent need for improved equipment, infrastructure, and professionalisation to ensure readiness and resilience in the face of current and future challenges.

a3076.speaker: Cristóvão Chume, Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.name: Cristóvão Chume
a3076.title: Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.speech: “The modernisation of the Armed Forces is a national priority. Equipment, infrastructure, culture, and greater professionalisation are the measures that will ensure our readiness and sustainability to face the challenges of the present and future.”

a3076.speaker: Cristóvão Chume, Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.name: Cristóvão Chume
a3076.title: Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.speech: Commended the discipline and loyalty of military personnel, particularly those deployed across various operational theatres ; “We are the silent heroes of the nation – the guarantors of territorial integrity, security, freedom, peace, and the foundation for national development” ; highlighted the role of the Defence and Security Forces in providing humanitarian assistance during natural disasters, describing them as “a shield for the nation.”

a3076.speaker: Cristóvão Chume, Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.name: Cristóvão Chume
a3076.title: Minister of Defence of Mozambique
a3076.speech: Said the commemoration week is also an opportunity to strengthen the bond between the Armed Forces and society, reflecting on their historical role in defending national unity and in the ongoing fight against terrorism in the Cabo Delgado province.

a3076.speaker: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (ACSS), an academic institution under the US Department of Defence
a3076.name: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (ACSS)
a3076.title: an academic institution under the US Department of Defence
a3076.speech: According to ACSS, at least 349 people were killed in terrorist attacks across northern Mozambique in 2024, representing a 36% increase compared to the previous year, with the majority of these attacks claimed by the Islamic State-affiliated extremist group.

a3261.speaker: Samuel Batcho, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a3261.name: Samuel Batcho
a3261.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin
a3261.speech: Said that this Legal Documentation and Information Centre, which will serve as a reference for land information for judges, has among its objectives the establishment of a single land management system and the establishment of a land code.

a3261.speaker: Melvin F. Williams Jr., Vice-President and General Counsel of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3261.name: Melvin F. Williams Jr.
a3261.title: Vice-President and General Counsel of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3261.speech: "MCA-Benin's progress has not gone unnoticed in Washington," he confided during the session in Cotonou ; He urged MCA-Benin officials and the contractors to redouble their efforts to meet the objectives set in the Compact, within the deadlines set, saying his greatest wish is the completion of the projects on schedule ; After the demonstration at the Ouidah court he said he was impressed by the existing potential in the area of justice in Benin, potential thanks to which Benin will be able to have a "very robust judicial system" once the courts under construction are completed and the Electronic Management Centre is operational.

a3286.speaker: Study by GRAIN and the Institute for Agriculture & Trade Policy
a3286.name: Study by GRAIN and the Institute for Agriculture & Trade Policy
a3286.speech: Finds that the profits of the world's nine largest fertilizer companies increased from around 14 billion dollars in 2020 to 28 billion dollars the following year – and then soared to 49 billion dollars last year.

a3286.speaker: United Nations
a3286.name: United Nations
a3286.speech: Warned in late 2022 that high fertiliser prices threaten to turn the current “crisis of affordability” into a “crisis of availability.”

a3286.speaker: Independent studies and evaluations commissioned by AGRA (Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa)
a3286.name: Independent studies and evaluations commissioned by AGRA (Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa)
a3286.speech: Have found that the organization is far from meeting its goals of doubling yields and incomes for millions of smallholder African farmers.

a3339.speaker: Ukrainian officials
a3339.name: Ukrainian officials
a3339.speech: Said Russia launched waves of missile and drone attacks on Kyiv before dawn on Thursday, killing at least eight people including a six-year-old boy, and wounding 88 others; officials said schools and hospitals were among the buildings damaged across 27 locations in the city.

a3339.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskiy, President of Ukraine
a3339.name: Volodymyr Zelenskiy
a3339.title: President of Ukraine
a3339.speech: Said Russia launched more than 300 drones and eight missiles: "Today the world has once again seen Russia's response to our desire for peace with America and Europe. Therefore, peace without strength is impossible," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app.

a3339.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskiy, President of Ukraine
a3339.name: Volodymyr Zelenskiy
a3339.title: President of Ukraine
a3339.speech: "The attack was extremely insidious and deliberately calculated to overload the air defence system," Zelenskiy wrote on X; he posted a video of burning ruins, saying people were still trapped under the rubble of one partially-ruined residential building as of the morning; the president said the attacks had killed a six-year-old and the boy's mother, but later edited the post to remove reference to the mother.

a3339.speaker: Russia's Defence Ministry
a3339.name: Russia's Defence Ministry
a3339.speech: Said it targeted and hit Ukrainian military airfields and ammunition depots as well as businesses linked to what it called Kyiv's military-industrial complex.

a3339.speaker: Vitali Klitschko, Mayor of Kyiv
a3339.name: Vitali Klitschko
a3339.title: Mayor of Kyiv
a3339.speech: Said nine children were wounded, the largest number hurt in a single night in the city since Russia started its full-scale invasion almost three and a half years ago.

a3339.speaker: Yurii Kravchuk, 62, Kyiv resident
a3339.name: Yurii Kravchuk
a3339.title: 62, Kyiv resident
a3339.speech: He had heard the missile alert but did not get to a shelter in time, he told Reuters: "I started waking up my wife and then there was an explosion. My daughter ended up in the hospital."

a3339.speaker: Ukraine's Ministry of Internal Affairs
a3339.name: Ukraine's Ministry of Internal Affairs
a3339.speech: Said rescuers spent more than three hours getting to a man trapped in rubble by cutting through the wall of a neighbouring apartment; he talked to the emergency services during the operation and was pulled out alive, it added.

a3339.speaker: Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv city military administration
a3339.name: Tymur Tkachenko
a3339.title: head of the Kyiv city military administration
a3339.speech: Said on national television that a five-month-old baby was among the wounded, with five children hospitalized.

a3339.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a3339.name: Donald Trump
a3339.title: U.S. President
a3339.speech: Said on Tuesday that the United States would start imposing tariffs and other measures on Russia "10 days from today" if Moscow showed no progress toward ending the conflict.

a3339.speaker: Yulia Svyrydenko, Prime Minister of Ukraine
a3339.name: Yulia Svyrydenko
a3339.title: Prime Minister of Ukraine
a3339.speech: "This is Putin's response to Trump's deadlines. The world must respond with a tribunal and maximum pressure."

a3339.speaker: Ukrainian air force
a3339.name: Ukrainian air force
a3339.speech: Reported five direct missile hits and 21 drone hits in 12 locations; Ukrainian air defence units downed 288 drones and three cruise missiles, the air force added.

a3461.speaker: Ida Sawyer, Crisis and Conflict Director of Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a3461.name: Ida Sawyer
a3461.title: Crisis and Conflict Director of Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a3461.speech: “HRW's investigation concluded that the attack led by Hamas on 7 October was designed to kill civilians and to abduct as many people as possible,” she indicated in the latest report.

a3461.speaker: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.name: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.speech: Concluded that Hamas commandos committed several crimes against humanity: targeting civilians, the deliberate killing of detained persons, cruel and inhuman treatment, sexual and gender-based violence, hostage-taking, mutilation and looting of corpses, use of human shields and pillaging ; recalled that the basic principle of humanitarian law is that all parties to a conflict must at all times distinguish between combatants and civilians, “who must never be the target of an attack” ; stressed that 815 of the 1,195 people killed that day were civilians, and that of the 251 abducted — of whom 116 remain in Gaza, 42 already dead — the majority are civilians ; stated that these acts were not “an afterthought, a failed plan or isolated acts,” having studied testimony from victims, relatives, rescue teams and medical experts as well as more than 280 photographs and videos of the assault ; said that in one of the videos militiamen can be seen actively searching out civilians and killing them, proving the intentionality of the attacks and that the hostage-taking was “planned and highly coordinated” ; said further investigation was needed to prove other crimes, such as persecution of identifiable groups on racial, ethnic or religious grounds, or rape and other acts of sexual violence.

a3461.speaker: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.name: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.speech: Stressed that Israel committed crimes against humanity by inflicting collective punishment on the population of the Gaza Strip after the attacks, through the cutting of essential services and the limiting of humanitarian aid entering the enclave, where more than 38,700 Palestinians have died in the military offensive since 7 October ; said this punishment “aggravates the impact of more than 17 years of Israel's illegal closure of Gaza,” and accused Israel of committing “crimes of 'apartheid' and persecution against the Palestinians.”

a3461.speaker: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.name: Human Rights Watch (report)
a3461.speech: Called on all parties to respect humanitarian law and on the Palestinian militias in Gaza to release “immediately and unconditionally the civilians they are holding as hostages” ; said: “They must take disciplinary measures against the members responsible for war crimes and hand over for prosecution any persons facing an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC).”

a3461.speaker: Hamas authorities (as reported by HRW)
a3461.name: Hamas authorities (as reported by HRW)
a3461.speech: “The Hamas authorities responded to HRW's questions, asserting that they had ordered their forces not to attack civilians and not to deviate from human rights and humanitarian law,” said HRW, which stated it “found evidence to the contrary.”

a3461.speaker: Prosecutor-General of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a3461.name: Prosecutor-General of the International Criminal Court (ICC)
a3461.speech: On 20 May issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, and Hamas leaders Yahya Sinwar, Ismail Haniyeh and Mohamed Deif.

a3467.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation
a3467.name: Vladimir Putin
a3467.title: President of the Russian Federation
a3467.speech: “The main objective is to strengthen the well-being of our citizens, to improve living conditions and to resolve urgent questions and problems,” declared the President of the Russian Federation, Vladimir Putin, at the opening of the Forum ; “Russia is sincerely interested in deepening humanitarian, commercial and investment relations with Africa,” the Russian president maintained ; announced at the Saint Petersburg Forum the implementation of 30 energy projects in 16 countries of the continent, adding: “we will pay particular attention to the delivery of wheat and maize to African countries.”

a3467.speaker: Azali Assoumani, President of the Union of the Comoros and current Chairman of the African Union
a3467.name: Azali Assoumani
a3467.title: President of the Union of the Comoros and current Chairman of the African Union
a3467.speech: Said this Forum was an opportunity to address major questions for the continent and to reaffirm the partnership with Russia: “It is obvious that Russia has every place to position itself as a major partner and we are ready to address with it all the big questions of cooperation,” explained the current chairman of the AU ; pleaded on behalf of his peers for the lifting of the suspension of Ukrainian wheat exports so that African countries that import this commodity may do so.

a3467.speaker: Dilma Rousseff, President of the BRICS Bank
a3467.name: Dilma Rousseff
a3467.title: President of the BRICS Bank
a3467.speech: Maintained that this new bank is ready to support promising initiatives in developing countries and especially those of Africa.

a3520.speaker: Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso (reported by Al Jazeera)
a3520.name: Mali
a3520.title: Niger and Burkina Faso (reported by Al Jazeera)
a3520.speech: According to Al Jazeera, the countries accused ECOWAS of taking directives “dictated to it by powers that are foreign to Africa”.

a3520.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a3520.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a3520.speech: According to UNHCR, the country is hosting over 69 847 Burkinabe political asylum seekers.

a3520.speaker: Arthur Mogorotsi, South African analyst
a3520.name: Arthur Mogorotsi
a3520.title: South African analyst
a3520.speech: President Ouattara of Côte d’Ivoire could serve as a key interlocutor in maintaining the relationship with France, according to South African analyst Arthur Mogorotsi.

a3578.speaker: Observatory of Economic Complexity (OEC) (trade data)
a3578.name: Observatory of Economic Complexity (OEC) (trade data)
a3578.speech: According to the latest data from the OEC, fruit juice generated E2.4 million, non-knit men's suits earned E1.6 million and other non-knit clothing accessories brought in E947 050 during the month; total exports to the UK rose to E5.8 million, a 154 per cent increase from E2.3 million in May 2024, while imports from the UK fell by 39.4 per cent to E2.2 million. Latest data also indicates that the leading agro-processing firm exports in 205-litre drums to juice processors who then process it into finished products.

a3578.speaker: UK Government (announcement of 10 July 2025)
a3578.name: UK Government (announcement of 10 July 2025)
a3578.speech: Unveiled upgrades to its Developing Countries Trading Scheme (DCTS), with the intention of simplifying access to the UK market for developing nations; Eswatini, along with 64 other countries, stands to benefit from enhanced trade access, tariff-free exports and targeted support in meeting international trade standards, and among the most impactful changes is the introduction of simplified rules of origin.

a3615.speaker: Alieu Badara, Gambian musician
a3615.name: Alieu Badara
a3615.title: Gambian musician
a3615.speech: Said in a recent interview, on his mission to revive fading cultural treasures: “Most of our local instruments are disappearing; you can only find them in the provinces now. This generation needs to connect with our culture and heritage.” ; “Our instruments represent our culture, traditions, and heritage. They define us and how we communicate with the world.”

a3615.speaker: Alieu Badara, Gambian musician
a3615.name: Alieu Badara
a3615.title: Gambian musician
a3615.speech: Admitted that the endeavor required significant time and resources, but expressed pride in the result: “It took a lot of work, but I’m satisfied.”

a3615.speaker: Alieu Badara, Gambian musician
a3615.name: Alieu Badara
a3615.title: Gambian musician
a3615.speech: On the new GamAfro genre, said he envisions it as a distinct identity for Gambian music and encouraged other artists to contribute to its evolution: “This is just the beginning,” expressing hope that the genre will grow and gain global recognition.

a3615.speaker: Alieu Badara, Gambian musician
a3615.name: Alieu Badara
a3615.title: Gambian musician
a3615.speech: His advice to aspiring musicians: “Music takes time, hard work, and dedication. Be patient, seize every opportunity, and carry your identity—it’s what makes you stand out.”

a3615.speaker: Dignitaries and executives at the Africa-U.S. Summit in Luanda, Angola
a3615.name: Dignitaries and executives at the Africa-U.S. Summit in Luanda
a3615.title: Angola
a3615.speech: Praised Badara’s performance, lauding his innovative approach and cultural advocacy.

a3701.speaker: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (Fewsnet) analysis
a3701.name: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (Fewsnet) analysis
a3701.speech: Analysis indicating that Malawi is experiencing a negative balance in maize supplies, with overall production 28 percent lower than the five-year average, and that informal imports have proven insufficient to offset this deficit ; indicates that the Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation (Admarc) and the National Food Reserve Agency (NFRA) have only managed to purchase less than 70,000MT, far below the 261,000MT required to meet the country's growing needs, including humanitarian assistance and subsidised commercial sales, and that the stock may be even lower ; further notes that the below-average maize supplies are driving food prices up, prompting Admarc to raise its maize prices in September from K600 to K790 per kilogramme—almost equal to or exceeding the prices set by private traders.

a3701.speaker: National Food Reserve Agency (NFRA)
a3701.name: National Food Reserve Agency (NFRA)
a3701.speech: Recently said that the agency has slightly over 60,000MT of maize in stock, which represents a 50 percent shortfall from the 120,000MT required for the strategic grain reserve.

a3701.speaker: Theresa Chapulapula, Admarc spokesperson
a3701.name: Theresa Chapulapula
a3701.title: Admarc spokesperson
a3701.speech: In an interview Tuesday, confirmed that the State grain trader has procured 32,000MT of maize.

a3701.speaker: Samuel Longwe, Economist
a3701.name: Samuel Longwe
a3701.title: Economist
a3701.speech: Said maize deficits could significantly impact inflation, as maize is a major component of the food basket: “Maize carries considerable weight in inflation calculations. The immediate solution would be to import more so that people have better access domestically. In the long term, we need to increase production.”

a3701.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3701.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a3701.title: President of Malawi
a3701.speech: On March 23, 2024, declared a state of disaster in 23 of Malawi's 28 districts in anticipation of a poor harvest due to the El Niño climatic event, which left over two million people in need of food assistance ; estimated that close to 600,000MT of maize, valued at K357.6 billion, would be required for the humanitarian response.

a3868.speaker: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, Prime Minister and acting Head of Government of Djibouti
a3868.name: Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed
a3868.title: Prime Minister and acting Head of Government of Djibouti
a3868.speech: Firmly requested Algeria's support for Djibouti's candidacy for the presidency of the African Commission.

a3868.speaker: Djibouti and Algeria (the two sides, in the meeting)
a3868.name: Djibouti and Algeria (the two sides
a3868.title: in the meeting)
a3868.speech: The discussions highlighted the economic and political integration of the African continent, with collaborative initiatives involving the Maghreb region, as well as cooperation in multilateral forums such as the African Union, the Arab League and the United Nations, to defend the two nations' common interests ; the two sides also discussed ways to increase bilateral trade, to promote cultural exchanges in order to consolidate ties between the peoples, as well as the economic diversification of Djibouti and Algeria, with emphasis on strategic sectors, notably agriculture and industry.

a3915.speaker: Economic resolution of the party and the government of 22 September 1960 (document)
a3915.name: Economic resolution of the party and the government of 22 September 1960 (document)
a3915.speech: Called, among other things: for an immediate and rigorous attack on economic decolonisation; for the rapid establishment of new economic structures by overturning and developing commercial circuits within the framework of socialist planning founded on African realities; for the use of every means to put in place a rail, road, river and air infrastructure in keeping with the country's needs — it was in application of these decisions that the national company Air Mali was created.

a3915.speaker: Colonel Assimi Souleymane Dembele (book, extract cited)
a3915.name: Colonel Assimi Souleymane Dembele (book
a3915.title: extract cited)
a3915.speech: His book shows an image of Mali that few people suspect — alongside the memory of great empires, another, more secret and less glorious Mali of bullying, torture and assassinations that nobody talks about; that from the "socialist" era of Modibo Keita to the long reign of the military under Moussa Traore these were thirty years of unspeakable violence in which no one was spared, neither women, nor children, nor old people, the chain of assassinations unbroken and the executioners unfailingly ending up as the victims, in the name of ideology and of power; it is on reading the book that one understands the price the country paid for its stability: a life made of silence.

a3915.speaker: Griots (in their Tarik)
a3915.name: Griots (in their Tarik)
a3915.speech: Teach that it belongs to the horons "tlobile" to lead Mali.

a3915.speaker: First conservative and traditionalist (anonymous)
a3915.name: First conservative and traditionalist (anonymous)
a3915.speech: "Pretentious peoples and youth, a day will come when this country will have as supreme chiefs only people of servile condition (slaves) to govern you."

a3915.speaker: Second conservative and traditionalist (anonymous)
a3915.name: Second conservative and traditionalist (anonymous)
a3915.speech: "If there are fifty-two (52) weeks in the year, it is not certain that the true noble families reach that number in Mali."

a3915.speaker: UNESCO (calculation cited)
a3915.name: UNESCO (calculation cited)
a3915.speech: In 1960 the school enrolment rate (UNESCO calculation) was still very low: 10%, and illiteracy reached 95% of the total population.

a4045.speaker: Africa CDC and WHO (joint Continental Response Plan)
a4045.name: Africa CDC and WHO (joint Continental Response Plan)
a4045.speech: have updated their joint Continental Response Plan for the mpox emergency as the disease continues to affect new areas. The revised strategy focuses on controlling outbreaks, while expanding vaccination coverage and transitioning toward a longer-term, sustainable response.

a4045.speaker: Africa CDC
a4045.name: Africa CDC
a4045.speech: declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security in August 2024 after clade Ib began spreading through sexual networks and within households and through close contact.

a4045.speaker: WHO Director-General
a4045.name: WHO Director-General
a4045.speech: declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024.

a4045.speaker: Updated Continental Response Plan (Africa CDC/WHO document)
a4045.name: Updated Continental Response Plan (Africa CDC/WHO document)
a4045.speech: calls for intensified efforts to bring outbreaks under control, while also taking concrete actions to integrate mpox into routine health services.

a4045.speaker: WHO (updated global strategic plan)
a4045.name: WHO (updated global strategic plan)
a4045.speech: has updated the global strategic plan to curb – and where feasible, to stop – human-to-human transmission of mpox.

a4131.speaker: Simon Shuster, Time senior correspondent for Ukraine and Russia (article)
a4131.name: Simon Shuster
a4131.title: Time senior correspondent for Ukraine and Russia (article)
a4131.speech: Asserts in his latest article that the Biden administration never intended to make Ukraine win: “When Russia invaded Ukraine nearly three years ago, President Joe Biden set three objectives for the American response. Ukraine's victory was never one of them” ; “[Zelensky's] appeals met with a mixed reception. On the question of Ukraine's NATO membership, Biden would not budge.”

a4131.speaker: Simon Shuster, Time senior correspondent for Ukraine and Russia (article)
a4131.name: Simon Shuster
a4131.title: Time senior correspondent for Ukraine and Russia (article)
a4131.speech: Describes Zelensky as delusional: “His belief in Ukraine's final victory over Russia has hardened and worries some of his advisers. It is unshakeable, bordering on messianism.”

a4131.speaker: One of Zelensky's closest aides (anonymous, quoted by Simon Shuster)
a4131.name: One of Zelensky's closest aides (anonymous
a4131.title: quoted by Simon Shuster)
a4131.speech: “He's deluding himself” ; “We have no more options. We are not winning. But try telling him that.”

a4131.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President (at the World Economic Forum in Davos)
a4131.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a4131.title: Ukrainian President (at the World Economic Forum in Davos)
a4131.speech: Asserted that Western promises to one day admit Ukraine into NATO were a “lie”, and that the United States and Germany maintained contacts with Russia throughout the war: “On the part of certain States, I think that at the outset it was not a very transparent policy, they did not support us in NATO. They did not support us in NATO and merely said that Ukraine would be part of NATO. That was not fair to Ukraine and Ukrainians. And it was not fair on the part of our leaders either. When some of our leaders said and promised that we would be in NATO, that was not fair either... I think that Germany and the United States adopted a position of weakness. Because they had a dialogue with the Russians. And I believe they lost that dialogue. We lost, because they always appeal to the fact that there were agreements with the Russians.”

a4131.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President (interview after his speech)
a4131.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a4131.title: Ukrainian President (interview after his speech)
a4131.speech: Asserts that at least 200,000 European peacekeepers will be needed to prevent a new Russian attack after any ceasefire agreement: “Of all the Europeans? Two hundred thousand, that's a minimum. That's a minimum, otherwise it's nothing.”

a4131.speaker: Strana (Ukrainian news outlet)
a4131.name: Strana (Ukrainian news outlet)
a4131.speech: Notes: “Let us recall that Zelensky himself asserted on several occasions that Ukraine would be part of NATO. Moreover, Kyiv is now demanding admission to the Alliance as a condition for making peace with Russia. At the same time, Zelensky admits that the United States and Germany are opposed to it.”

a4131.speaker: Alexey Arestovich, former adviser to Zelensky
a4131.name: Alexey Arestovich
a4131.title: former adviser to Zelensky
a4131.speech: Responds to Zelensky's assertion: “What are you saying? Who is the main person responsible for the massive spread of this lie to Ukrainians, for the persecution of those who said that there would be no NATO, that it is a swindle, that we are being deceived, and that we signed up to sacrifice our lives for it — do you have the strength to name him?”

a4131.speaker: Professor Glenn Diesen
a4131.name: Professor Glenn Diesen
a4131.speech: Adds: “The Western media are also responsible: Anyone opposing the setting up and sacrifice of Ukrainians in the framework of a proxy war was called a propagandist for Russia. Only vile and relentless war propaganda was allowed in the media.”

a4131.speaker: RAND Corporation, 2019 report on “overextending” Russia (Pentagon think tank)
a4131.name: RAND Corporation
a4131.title: 2019 report on “overextending” Russia (Pentagon think tank)
a4131.speech: Found that the most favourable way to “overextend Russia” was to use Ukraine in a war against it by providing lethal weapons: “The United States could increase its military assistance to Ukraine — in terms of the quantity and quality of weapons... The United States could also more vigorously support Ukraine's accession to NATO. While NATO's unanimity requirement makes Ukraine's membership unlikely in the foreseeable future, Washington's insistence on this possibility could strengthen Ukraine's resolve while leading Russia to redouble its efforts to prevent such a development” ; the report also lists risks: “Russia could also provoke a counter-escalation by committing more troops and pushing them deeper into Ukraine... It could result in a disproportionate number of Ukrainian casualties, territorial losses and refugee flows. It could even lead Ukraine to a disadvantageous peace.”

a4131.speaker: Former US officials (anonymous, cited report on CIA–Ukraine cooperation)
a4131.name: Former US officials (anonymous
a4131.title: cited report on CIA–Ukraine cooperation)
a4131.speech: “The partnership saw the CIA help Ukraine rebuild its Main Intelligence Directorate, known by the acronym HUR, which became famous for its daring operations. The CIA ultimately devoted millions of dollars to training and equipping Ukrainian intelligence officers, as well as to building facilities, notably a dozen secret forward operating bases on the border with Russia. The two services also began conducting joint operations together around the world, the highest level of trust for intelligence services, according to the former US officials.”

a4131.speaker: French Defence Ministry (2020 estimate)
a4131.name: French Defence Ministry (2020 estimate)
a4131.speech: Cited as the source that the entire French armed forces numbered a little over 200,000 in 2020.

a4216.speaker: Godswill Obong Akpabio, Senate President of Nigeria
a4216.name: Godswill Obong Akpabio
a4216.title: Senate President of Nigeria
a4216.speech: Summoned the Directors General of the NIA, DIA, DSS and the National Security Adviser to brief senators on the alleged involvement of USAID in the sponsorship of Boko Haram: “I am convening an emergency closed session with the National Security Adviser, Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, Director-General of the Department of State Services, and Director-General of the Defence Intelligence Agency to provide an immediate briefing on the allegations surrounding USAID’s funding of Boko Haram in Nigeria. We must get to the bottom of this matter, and I expect a thorough and transparent briefing from our national security leadership.” ; said it is only through thorough investigation that the truth can be established, adding that even if America has not taken an obligation hook, line and sinker, Nigeria must also investigate to be sure: “Because we won’t just keep quiet. If it is true that USAID has been funding Boko Haram in Nigeria. We have no business allowing them to have offices in Nigeria and before we can take decisive steps and also ask for recompense in particular, we must go deeper into the issue. So it’s important that we get briefed by our intelligence community.”

a4216.speaker: Ali Ndume, Senator (mover of the motion)
a4216.name: Ali Ndume
a4216.title: Senator (mover of the motion)
a4216.speech: Presenting the motion before the Senate, noted that on Thursday, 13th February 2025, the entire social media space was agog with a trending video of United States Republican Congressman Scott Perry alleging that USAID has been funding terrorist organisations across the world, Boko Haram inclusive ; said this allegation is coming on the heels of the Chief of Defence Staff raising an alarm that Boko Haram terrorist groups are being sponsored and trained by international organisations ; noted that over the years the modus operandi of Boko Haram in Nigeria has been a source of great concern and their source of funding and operations have been shrouded in mystery ; said the monumental devastation caused by Boko Haram has dented the image of the country among the comity of nations and that there is an urgent need for steps to be taken by the Federal Government to unravel the mystery behind this whole episode.

a4216.speaker: Scott Perry, United States Republican Congressman representing Pennsylvania (social-media video of subcommittee hearing)
a4216.name: Scott Perry
a4216.title: United States Republican Congressman representing Pennsylvania (social-media video of subcommittee hearing)
a4216.speech: Alleged at the inaugural hearing of the subcommittee on delivering on government efficiency that USAID has been funding terrorist organisations across the world, Boko Haram inclusive.

a4216.speaker: General Christopher Musa, Chief of Defence Staff of Nigeria
a4216.name: General Christopher Musa
a4216.title: Chief of Defence Staff of Nigeria
a4216.speech: Raised an alarm that Boko Haram terrorist groups are being sponsored and trained by international organisations.

a4216.speaker: Abdul Ningi, Senator (co-sponsor of the motion)
a4216.name: Abdul Ningi
a4216.title: Senator (co-sponsor of the motion)
a4216.speech: Said it’s almost impossible to do justice to the issues raised by this motion unless the top brass of the security sector are invited to brief the Senate: “The Senate needs to be briefed, first and foremost, by the heads of various security agencies in a closed-door session. I also don’t want this in the media because beyond the media, beyond what I know, beyond what you know, we have intelligence organisation, that is funded by this government.”

a4233.speaker: Trump administration
a4233.name: Trump administration
a4233.speech: On Monday welcomed a small group of white South Africans as refugees, saying they face discrimination and violence at home.

a4233.speaker: Refugee advocates
a4233.name: Refugee advocates
a4233.speech: Have raised questions about why the group should be admitted when the Trump administration has suspended efforts to resettle people who are fleeing war and persecution and have gone through years of vetting before coming to the United States.

a4233.speaker: Christopher Landau, US Deputy Secretary of State
a4233.name: Christopher Landau
a4233.title: US Deputy Secretary of State
a4233.speech: “I want you all to know that you are really welcome here and that we respect what you have had to deal with these last few years” ; “We respect the long tradition of your people and what you have accomplished over the years.”

a4233.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4233.name: Donald Trump
a4233.title: US President
a4233.speech: Told reporters earlier Monday that he’s admitting them as refugees because of the “genocide that’s taking place.” He said that in post-apartheid South Africa, white farmers are “being killed” and he plans to address the issue with South African leadership next week.

a4233.speaker: Government of South Africa
a4233.name: Government of South Africa
a4233.speech: Strongly denies that white South Africans face discrimination and violence at home; says the U.S. allegations that the white minority Afrikaners are being persecuted are “completely false,” the result of misinformation and an inaccurate view of its country; cited the fact that Afrikaners are among the richest and most successful people in the country and said they are among “the most economically privileged.”

a4233.speaker: Experts in South Africa and an Afrikaner group
a4233.name: Experts in South Africa and an Afrikaner group

a4233.speaker: Conservative commentators
a4233.name: Conservative commentators
a4233.speech: Have promoted the allegation about a genocide against white farmers in South Africa.

a4233.speaker: Elon Musk, South African-born Trump ally
a4233.name: Elon Musk
a4233.title: South African-born Trump ally
a4233.speech: Has posted on social media that some politicians in the country are “actively promoting white genocide.”

a4463.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID Mission Director
a4463.name: Helen Pataki
a4463.title: USAID Mission Director
a4463.speech: Said, “USAID is committed to protecting lives and livelihoods, and reducing the impact of disasters on vulnerable populations by helping households and communities in Mozambique. USAID is proud to work with IOM to provide these supplies to meet the needs of affected Mozambicans.”

a4463.speaker: Dr. Laura Tomm-Bonde, IOM Mozambique Chief of Mission
a4463.name: Dr. Laura Tomm-Bonde
a4463.title: IOM Mozambique Chief of Mission
a4463.speech: Said, “IOM with the support of its partners aims to manage the effects of displacement by assisting the most vulnerable populations across Mozambique. This significant contribution from USAID will go a long way; it is greatly needed and appreciated and contributes to IOM’s aim to ensure aid is provided to help meet the urgent needs of those most affected by displacement”.

a4463.speaker: DTM Baseline Round 15, February 2022 (IOM data)
a4463.name: DTM Baseline Round 15
a4463.title: February 2022 (IOM data)
a4463.speech: Cited as the source for the displacement of more than 784,564 people in Mozambique, mostly in the central and northern region.

a4463.speaker: Humanitarian Response Plan, 2022
a4463.name: Humanitarian Response Plan
a4463.speech: Cited as the source for the estimate that 1.5 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance.

a4463.speaker: IOM Mozambique Roadmap for northern Mozambique
a4463.name: IOM Mozambique Roadmap for northern Mozambique
a4463.speech: Cited as the source for IOM’s 2022 funding requirements of USD 79.3 million to continue and scale up its Humanitarian, Development and Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach in northern Mozambique.

a4465.speaker: USAID (announcement)
a4465.name: USAID (announcement)
a4465.speech: Announced the suspension of new funding and of disbursements under Development Objective Agreements (DOAGs) until the review of USAID-funded country assistance programmes is completed, within 85 days starting from January 24, 2025.

a4465.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a4465.name: Government of Tanzania
a4465.speech: Said it is strengthening itself to ensure it grows the economy by using [domestic] sources of funds and revenue to fill in the areas that have been reduced.

a4465.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a4465.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a4465.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a4465.speech: Said the Government is strengthening itself to grow the economy using the resources available so as to afford implementation in all the important areas, including the health, education and water sectors ; said Tanzania respects foreign affairs policies and implements those agreements as agreed with the countries concerned: “We have begun to see countries with great capacity, including the United States, and these changes affect some countries, and even ours may suffer some effects, but for us it is important to observe foreign policies as we have agreed.” ; “We have the capacity, we have natural resources, we have resources; the task we have is for Tanzanians to work together to ensure that we use the natural resources and resources we have to build the domestic economy so as to enable the plans and budgets to implement these things.” ; “For us, along with the breadth of the relations we have established, the point is to ensure that we strengthen ourselves and have domestic capacity. We must strengthen ourselves in our plans; our budgets must be able to implement all the important areas, including the health, education and water sectors and other areas, in accordance with what has been agreed with the countries concerned.” ; “Let me say that the United States has already announced, and it is possible that other countries may also announce that there will be changes, and we are continuing to strengthen ourselves by ensuring that we grow our economy using [our own] sources of funds and revenue. We put it together and bring it here to Parliament so that a work plan is drawn up so that we can fill in the areas that have been reduced; that is the strategy we now need to have.”

a4465.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a4465.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a4465.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a4465.speech: Congratulated President Samia Suluhu Hassan for continuing to make Tanzania maintain good relations with many countries in the world, including the United States.

a4465.speaker: George Mwanisongole, Member of Parliament for Mbozi
a4465.name: George Mwanisongole
a4465.title: Member of Parliament for Mbozi
a4465.speech: Asked how the Government is preparing to deal with the changes in United States foreign policy which are going to affect the implementation of Tanzania's policies in several areas, including education and health: “How is the Government preparing for the changing policies of the United States, which, since President Donald Trump came to power, has made major changes to its foreign policy that are going to affect the implementation of our policies in education, health and the economy.” ; named the affected USAID-funded projects as the Education Program for Results (EP4R) project and the programme to reduce the severity of HIV.

a4465.speaker: Parliament of Tanzania (resolution, February 4, 2025)
a4465.name: Parliament of Tanzania (resolution
a4465.title: February 4, 2025)
a4465.speech: Resolved that the Government should implement a plan to obtain domestic resources to fight HIV infection and AIDS without depending on donor aid.

a4465.speaker: Elibariki Kingu, Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs
a4465.name: Elibariki Kingu
a4465.title: Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs
a4465.speech: Said that a large proportion of the implementation of HIV and AIDS interventions in the country depends on donor funds from outside the country: “If that funding comes to an end, it could to a large extent cause the country to slow down the pace of fighting that scourge for lack of sufficient funds.”

a4519.speaker: Femi Babafemi, NDLEA (National Drug Law Enforcement Agency) spokesperson (statement)
a4519.name: Femi Babafemi
a4519.title: NDLEA (National Drug Law Enforcement Agency) spokesperson (statement)
a4519.speech: Released a statement on Sunday detailing a string of major operations conducted between July 7 and 12, 2025, targeting smuggling rings operating within and outside the country ; the statement said: "Izugha came under NDLEA radar on 7th August 2024 after a 9kg cocaine was recovered from a suspect Obiora Joseph Agudosi, at a motor park in Orile, Lagos while going to deliver the consignment in the southeast. Izugha was identified as the owner of the seized drug."

a4974.speaker: Study published in The Lancet (researchers)
a4974.name: Study published in The Lancet (researchers)
a4974.speech: Found that the move by USAID to cut financial assistance could cause more than 14 million deaths worldwide by 2030; warned that the effects could be seen in the fight against diseases such as HIV/AIDS, malaria and others including diarrhoea, and among young children; analysed mortality data from 133 low- and middle-income countries from 2001 to 2021 and found that USAID-backed health programmes prevented approximately 91.8 million deaths over those two decades; modelling suggests the current wave of funding cuts could wipe out that progress, potentially causing between 1.78 million and 2.5 million additional deaths each year between 2025 and 2030; found USAID-supported programmes were associated with a 15 percent reduction in all-cause deaths, and twice that (32 percent) for children under five, with a 65 percent reduction in HIV/AIDS deaths in countries receiving high levels of support and deaths from malaria and neglected tropical diseases falling by half; attributed a reduction of nearly two-thirds in HIV/AIDS-related deaths, about 25.5 million people, to USAID's work, and credited programmes on malaria, diarrhoeal diseases, neglected tropical diseases and lower respiratory infections with saving another 31 million lives.

a4974.speaker: Davide Rasella, co-author, Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal)
a4974.name: Davide Rasella
a4974.title: co-author, Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal)
a4974.speech: "This absence of funding could bring about one of the greatest obstacles to global health in several decades" ; "There is a risk of causing millions of preventable deaths, especially among the most vulnerable, and of reversing progress in health and in economic and social development," he added.

a4974.speaker: Germany, the United Kingdom and France (donor governments)
a4974.name: Germany
a4974.title: the United Kingdom and France (donor governments)
a4974.speech: After USAID reduced its assistance, several other major donors including Germany, the United Kingdom and France followed by announcing plans to cut their foreign aid budgets.

a4974.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4974.name: Marco Rubio
a4974.title: US Secretary of State
a4974.speech: Told Congress in March this year that 83 percent of USAID projects would be terminated, with the remainder merged into the State Department.

a4974.speaker: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., US Health Secretary
a4974.name: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
a4974.title: US Health Secretary
a4974.speech: Announced last week the halting of Washington's contribution of $300 million each year to Gavi, the international vaccine organisation which historically was channelled through USAID.

a4974.speaker: Reuters news agency
a4974.name: Reuters news agency
a4974.speech: Said that of the estimated more than 14 million people, one third of them young children, they could die as a result of the dismantling of America's international aid by the Trump administration.

a4974.speaker: Elon Musk, then close adviser to Donald Trump
a4974.name: Elon Musk
a4974.title: then close adviser to Donald Trump
a4974.speech: Two weeks after Trump returned to the White House, boasted about what he said was putting the agency 'through the wood chipper'.

a4979.speaker: Philip Gourevitch, author of a book on the Rwandan genocide
a4979.name: Philip Gourevitch
a4979.title: author of a book on the Rwandan genocide
a4979.speech: wrote: "The dead of Rwanda accumulated at nearly three times the rate of Jewish dead during the Holocaust. It was the most efficient mass killing since the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki."

a4979.speaker: United Nations Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, Resolution 260A(III) (document)
a4979.name: United Nations Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
a4979.title: Resolution 260A(III) (document)
a4979.speech: obliges contracting parties to "undertake to prevent and punish... acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial or religious group."

a4979.speaker: US government
a4979.name: US government
a4979.speech: opposed the use of the term "genocide" during the slaughter of the Tutsis, and even forbade its officials from calling the extermination genocide, even though it knew that "acts of genocide" were taking place.

a4979.speaker: Jane Hunter
a4979.name: Jane Hunter
a4979.speech: pointed out that "the media seldom wavered from their habitual racist portrayal of African strife as atavistic tribal savagery".

a4979.speaker: Francois Mitterrand, then French president
a4979.name: Francois Mitterrand
a4979.title: then French president
a4979.speech: said: "In such countries, genocide is not too important."

a4979.speaker: John Berry and Carol Berry, historians
a4979.name: John Berry and Carol Berry
a4979.title: historians
a4979.speech: pointed out: "The Belgians played a decisive role by imposing European racial stereotypes, supporting the Tutsis to the detriment of the Hutus, and then shifting the blame for colonial oppression to the Tutsis and leaving them to their fate."

a4979.speaker: Gregory Stanton, professor of genocide studies and prevention at George Mason University (Journal of Genocide Research)
a4979.name: Gregory Stanton
a4979.title: professor of genocide studies and prevention at George Mason University (Journal of Genocide Research)
a4979.speech: wrote that a lack of political will and geopolitical interests as well as racism influenced the decisions of Western powers regarding Rwanda: "Although the US and Britain were willing to commit soldiers and billions to save lives in Bosnia, where people are white, and the war was close to the interests of the European community, they were unwilling to do so in Rwanda, where people are black and the country has no strategic or economic interests."

a4979.speaker: Romeo Dallaire, Canadian General who commanded the UN force in Rwanda
a4979.name: Romeo Dallaire
a4979.title: Canadian General who commanded the UN force in Rwanda
a4979.speech: suggested in a 2004 speech at Butare University that racist stereotypes led to the international community's indifference: "Superpowers had no interest in you. They were interested in [the former] Yugoslavia. Thousands upon thousands (of) soldiers were sent there. The guiding principle was that in Rwanda it was tribalism, it was history repeating itself. In Yugoslavia, it was different - it was 400 years of historic conflict between great religions of the world. It was ethnic cleansing. It was European security. It was whites! Rwanda was black. It was in the middle of Africa. It had no strategic value."

a5133.speaker: Ethiopian News Agency (ENA)
a5133.name: Ethiopian News Agency (ENA)
a5133.speech: According to ENA, the flight used Bole International Airport (BIO) as a departure point and was reported to return to the same airport.

a5133.speaker: Ethiopian foreign ministry (statement on Twitter)
a5133.name: Ethiopian foreign ministry (statement on Twitter)
a5133.speech: “Ethiopia appreciates WFP initiative to launch humanitarian flights to Mekelle from Addis Ababa as per the guidelines set by the gov't. The gov't is committed to work closely w/ humanitarians who can provide concrete support to the people of Tigray.”

a5172.speaker: Michael Gonzales, US Ambassador to Zambia
a5172.name: Michael Gonzales
a5172.title: US Ambassador to Zambia
a5172.speech: Said the United States will cut $50 million in annual medical funding to Zambia over its weak response to the alleged theft and sale of donated drugs meant to be provided for free. The US embassy had in 2024 demanded Lusaka act on “the systemic theft of life-saving medicines and other products that were intended for free for the Zambian public” ; “Instead of investigating supply sources and pursuing the masterminds behind the theft of medicines, law enforcement operations have focused on low-level actors and have led to the arrest of only a few mid-level officials” ; the “United States can no longer justify to the American taxpayer continuing to provide such massive levels of assistance when the Zambian government will not take the necessary measures to protect this American investment” ; said the fraud was discovered in late 2021 and an inspection at more than 2,000 pharmacies last year had found that most were selling stolen goods, including products the United States provided for free ; said the cuts he announced were separate from a broader review of foreign aid spending by the administration of President Donald Trump ; asked if the action, to apply from January 2026, could be undone if the government took more action, the ambassador said: “At this point, after three years of raising it and one year of intensive engagement and requests, we have made this decision.”

a5172.speaker: Zambian health ministry
a5172.name: Zambian health ministry
a5172.speech: There was no immediate comment from the health ministry.

a5172.speaker: Washington (US government figures)
a5172.name: Washington (US government figures)
a5172.speech: About one-third of Zambia's public health spending comes from the United States, according to Washington.

a5504.speaker: Documents obtained by the New York Times (PEPFAR planning documents)
a5504.name: Documents obtained by the New York Times (PEPFAR planning documents)
a5504.speech: Revealed that the US government has begun mapping out plans to shut down the programme, and that the government has drafted a new plan to shift the programme from one that provides medicines and services to treat and prevent the spread of HIV in low-income countries to one centred on “bilateral relationships” with developing countries; according to the PEPFAR documents, the programme will focus instead on detecting outbreaks that could pose a threat to the United States and creating new markets for American drugs and technologies.

a5504.speaker: PEPFAR planning document
a5504.name: PEPFAR planning document
a5504.speech: Reads, “With targeted investment, PEPFAR's H.I.V. control capabilities in these countries could be transformed into a platform for rapid detection and outbreak response to protect Americans from disease threats like Ebola.”

a5504.speaker: The New York Times
a5504.name: The New York Times
a5504.speech: Reports that this progress may be cut short, only a few days after the US Congress moved to exempt the anti-AIDS programme from the major foreign aid cut ; reveals that the version it obtained shows input from numerous senior figures within the programme, including comments and revisions.

a5504.speaker: Official of the State Department (anonymous)
a5504.name: Official of the State Department (anonymous)
a5504.speech: Said the document had not been finalised: “The referenced document is not reflective of the State Department's policy on PEPFAR and was never cleared by Department leadership.”

a5504.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a5504.name: Marco Rubio
a5504.title: US Secretary of State
a5504.speech: Said the programme has been plagued by fraud and waste, necessitating the policies introduced by the Trump administration; he, however, insisted that, despite the reduced budget, all essential and life-saving services will continue.

a5650.speaker: Princeton University study, “Trends in Online Foreign Influence Efforts”
a5650.name: Princeton University study
a5650.title: “Trends in Online Foreign Influence Efforts”
a5650.speech: Revealed that Russia is the global leader in using online disinformation during influence campaigns, and that Russia is responsible for 62 per cent of such interference in the internal affairs of other countries.

a5650.speaker: High-ranking Russian officials at the Russian State Duma roundtable “Russia-Africa”
a5650.name: High-ranking Russian officials at the Russian State Duma roundtable “Russia-Africa”
a5650.speech: Emphasised the importance of “delivering truthful Russian news to African information spaces”; presented Russia as the nation entrusted with the “noble mission of putting an end to information colonialism in Africa.”

a5650.speaker: Damilola Banjo (report)
a5650.name: Damilola Banjo (report)
a5650.speech: States that incidents of people waving Russian flags have already occurred in Nigeria; in particular, demonstrators in Kano not only waved Russian flags but also called on Russia to pressure the Nigerian government into changing its policies.

a5650.speaker: Russia (official stance)
a5650.name: Russia (official stance)
a5650.speech: Denied any involvement in the events in Kano. ; After the annexation of Crimea and the invasion of Luhansk and Donetsk, Russia's official stance remained: “This is not Russia. These are ‘little green men.’ These are ‘unknown individuals.’”

a5650.speaker: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (funded by the US Congress)
a5650.name: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (funded by the US Congress)
a5650.speech: Has reported that Russia is the largest sponsor of disinformation campaigns on the continent; in 2022 the centre found that pro-Russian actors used thousands of new, fake, and hacked accounts to spread pro-Russian narratives and manipulate social media algorithms, leading to two pro-Russian hashtags trending on X/Twitter. According to the centre's report, the campaign aimed to create the appearance of global support ahead of the UN General Assembly vote in early March 2022 on a resolution condemning Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

a5650.speaker: Seigel
a5650.name: Seigel
a5650.speech: “This is clearly an attempt to stir unrest and manipulate genuine grievances [against the government]” ; “Protests are a normal democratic act to demand change. These are precisely the acts that are seized upon by an external actor… which has become a key way for Russia to enter and exert influence in Africa.”

a5650.speaker: Ihor Solovey, head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.name: Ihor Solovey
a5650.title: head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.speech: Says one of Ukraine's successful cases in countering hostile informational threats is the establishment of a structured approach to commenting on events: “From the first days of the war, the only officials authorised to comment on military events were the president, the chief of the General Staff, the commander-in-chief, the minister of defense, and the minister of foreign affairs. This hierarchy extended to the media, and no other figures commented on events directly related to military operations.”

a5650.speaker: Ihor Solovey, head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.name: Ihor Solovey
a5650.title: head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.speech: On the “United News” telethon: “Despite criticism, for the first year and a half, it mobilised the information space and society, preventing the opening of a new front and strengthening Ukrainian unity. For these reasons, its duration has been set until the end of martial law.”

a5650.speaker: Ihor Solovey, head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.name: Ihor Solovey
a5650.title: head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.speech: Emphasises that fighting disinformation is not only a matter of legal regulation but also media community awareness: “We do not have military censorship as such, so self-censorship has worked due to the high level of responsibility among journalists who understand that their material has a cost. And that cost is not only in monetary terms for an article or a report but also in human lives. The high level of media awareness is one of the phenomena of these years of war.”

a5650.speaker: Ihor Solovey, head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.name: Ihor Solovey
a5650.title: head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.speech: On engagement with foreign journalists: “This is a matter of strategic communication. Ukraine has never before hosted as many foreign journalists as it does now. The interest of international media, especially at the beginning of the full-scale war, was enormous. We worked hard to improve interaction with these media and developed an effective system.”

a5650.speaker: Ihor Solovey, head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.name: Ihor Solovey
a5650.title: head of the Center for Strategic Communications
a5650.speech: On Ukraine's shortcomings: “Alongside traditional media, which are reputable, have editorial offices, employ journalists, verify information, and maintain professional standards, a new media empire has emerged—social networks and news-sharing platforms. These are often anonymous sources, and the problem is that people tend to trust them more than official sources. This is our shortcoming.” ; “When working with these platforms, we face challenges. Some act responsibly and engage in dialogue, while others are less accountable, turning their platforms into hubs for disinformation. One of our shortcomings is that the state has not taken more decisive action against these networks and has not shut them down in Ukraine, as it previously did with Russia's VKontakte and Odnoklassniki. Instead, the government has issued recommendations, but this approach has not been fully effective.”

a5650.speaker: Olha Danchenkova, media expert
a5650.name: Olha Danchenkova
a5650.title: media expert
a5650.speech: Writes that it is also crucial to build trust with the audience and understand their expectations and fears before adversaries exploit them to undermine democratic institutions.

a5658.speaker: Rand Merchant Bank, “Where to Invest in Africa 2025/2026” report (compiled with the Gordon Institute of Business Science)
a5658.name: Rand Merchant Bank
a5658.title: “Where to Invest in Africa 2025/2026” report (compiled with the Gordon Institute of Business Science)
a5658.speech: Reports that Tanzania has overtaken Kenya as East Africa's most attractive investment destination, climbing three spots to ninth in Africa; that Tanzania's success is anchored in a persistent focus on foundational economics; and that investors frequently cite regulatory complexity, particularly around land tenure and licensing, and the need for deeper and more liquid capital markets as key headwinds that could slow investment momentum despite the strong macro picture.

a5658.speaker: A regional economist at a Johannesburg-based investment bank (anonymous)
a5658.name: A regional economist at a Johannesburg-based investment bank (anonymous)
a5658.speech: “Tanzania has mastered the art of providing a stable, predictable platform for megaprojects” ; “For major infrastructure funds, that certainty is worth more than a quick return in a volatile market.”

a5658.speaker: Isaah Mhlanga, RMB chief economist
a5658.name: Isaah Mhlanga
a5658.title: RMB chief economist
a5658.speech: Noted that the island nations stood out in a year marked by significant geopolitical shifts, including US trade tariffs and policy changes stemming from a number of elections across the region: “Episodes of unrest and policy uncertainty, and the global fracturing and reorientation have all had measurable macroeconomic effects” ; “Changes in the political and the subsequent policy environment and declining foreign aid, coupled with the redirection of global capital flows, are reshaping how African economies engage with the world.”

a5865.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a5865.name: Donald Trump
a5865.title: US President (executive order)
a5865.speech: Issued an executive order on Wednesday hitting India with an additional 25% tariff over its purchases of Russian oil; the new rate shall be "effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time 21 days after the date of this order."

a5865.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5865.name: Donald Trump
a5865.title: US President
a5865.speech: Had earlier warned he would raise levies, saying India "don't care how many people in Ukraine are being killed by the Russian War Machine."

a5865.speaker: White House (statement)
a5865.name: White House (statement)
a5865.speech: "The Russian Federation's actions in Ukraine pose an ongoing threat to US national security and foreign policy, necessitating stronger measures to address the national emergency" ; "India's importation of Russian Federation oil undermines US efforts to counter Russia's harmful activities."

a5865.speaker: New Delhi (Government of India)
a5865.name: New Delhi (Government of India)
a5865.speech: Had previously called Trump's threat to raise tariffs over its purchase of oil from Russia "unjustified and unreasonable."

a5865.speaker: Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India's foreign ministry
a5865.name: Randhir Jaiswal
a5865.title: spokesperson for India's foreign ministry
a5865.speech: Said the US had encouraged India to import Russian gas at the start of the conflict, "for strengthening global energy markets stability" ; said India "began importing from Russia because traditional supplies were diverted to Europe after the outbreak of the conflict."

a5963.speaker: Barthelemy Kassa, Minister of Mines and Energy of Benin (for the government)
a5963.name: Barthelemy Kassa
a5963.title: Minister of Mines and Energy of Benin (for the government)
a5963.speech: Says the Maria-Gleta power plant is working.

a5963.speaker: An agent of the Sbee (Beninese Electrical Energy Company) present on the site
a5963.name: An agent of the Sbee (Beninese Electrical Energy Company) present on the site
a5963.speech: “Any malfunction is visible on the computer and the alert is automatically given.”

a5963.speaker: Technicians of Cai and Sbee met on the Maria-Gleta site
a5963.name: Technicians of Cai and Sbee met on the Maria-Gleta site
a5963.speech: Said the system as installed and secured is capable of supplying, in Benin’s climatic conditions, around 65 megawatts, at a rate of 8.5 megawatts per turbine.

a5963.speaker: Head of the construction company (Cai)
a5963.name: Head of the construction company (Cai)
a5963.speech: Said the Maria-Gleta plant, costing 33 billion — the company’s figures — is “up to standard and meets the contractual conditions.”

a5963.speaker: Technicians of Cai
a5963.name: Technicians of Cai
a5963.speech: Said it is the difficulty of natural gas availability that forced Sbee, the plant’s operating company, to sign an insurance contract covering only five of the seven turbines received to date by the government, and that only for four hours a day.

a5963.speaker: Specialists (unnamed)
a5963.name: Specialists (unnamed)
a5963.speech: Said peak consumption is between 7 pm and 11 pm, and that it is in that time slot that, on Sbee’s orders, Cai starts up the turbines, whose number cannot exceed five for insurance reasons.

a5963.speaker: A Cai official
a5963.name: A Cai official
a5963.speech: Explained: “That means that when Ceb has a problem on its network (as was the case last Thursday), there is also a blackout — a cut,” and reported on talks under way for Cai to install its own network.

a5982.speaker: International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) policy report, co-authored by National Planning Commission (NPC) researchers
a5982.name: International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) policy report
a5982.title: co-authored by National Planning Commission (NPC) researchers
a5982.speech: Warns that the sudden withdrawal of US support could cost the Malawian economy more than $1.3 billion in cumulative gross domestic product (GDP) losses over the next six years and push 435,000 additional people into poverty by 2030 if corrective measures are not taken; estimates that the US disbursed over $431 million in official development assistance in 2023, accounting for a quarter of the country’s total aid and more than three percent of its gross national income, and indicates that annual foreign assistance disbursements have averaged over $360 million between 2020 and 2023 ; “The scale and suddenness of these cuts have exposed Malawi’s vulnerability. The country lacks economic buffers to withstand such a shock, making the consequences especially severe.”

a5982.speaker: IFPRI study (economy-wide modelling)
a5982.name: IFPRI study (economy-wide modelling)
a5982.speech: Predicted a 1 percent GDP decline in 2025—roughly $127 million—compared to a baseline scenario without aid reductions; foreign exchange inflows are expected to fall by $177 million, equivalent to 6.3 percent of Malawi’s merchandise import bill ; “The combination of reduced aid-financed activity and loss of foreign exchange is squeezing both public services and private sector operations. The result is lower productivity, higher costs and increased poverty.” ; Health programmes, which received 57 percent of US bilateral aid in 2023, are the hardest hit, with an estimated 48 to 51 percent of US-funded health programmes terminated or suspended, including nearly all maternal and child health initiatives.

a5982.speaker: United Nations Aids Programme (UNAIDS)
a5982.name: United Nations Aids Programme (UNAIDS)
a5982.speech: As of March 2025, more than 4,400 health workers had lost their jobs and 18 HIV drop-in centres were shut down, according to United Nations Aids Programme.

a5982.speaker: IFPRI economists / the report’s authors
a5982.name: IFPRI economists / the report’s authors
a5982.speech: Are imploring the Malawi Government to adopt a more flexible exchange rate and introduce trade facilitation reforms to cushion the blow, estimating that cumulative GDP losses could be reduced by 26 percent and poverty impacts nearly halved; also call for improved integration of donor-funded services into national systems, better targeting of essential services and diversification of funding sources to reduce reliance on any single donor ; “Increased fiscal space can help the government better address unexpected shocks. Currently, high fiscal deficits are driven in large part by statutory expenditures and insufficient revenues. However, there is already significant scope to improve public finances by increasing tax collection and improving the efficiency and efficacy of public expenditures.”

a6105.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6105.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6105.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6105.speech: Expresses serious disdain and frustration at the United States Millennium Challenge Corporation's (MCC) immediate pause, amid Liberia's eligibility, noting that it is clear the country may no longer hope and rely on the MCC as a priority; speaking on the midnight talk show The Heat, disclosed that when news about Liberia's eligibility for the MCC was announced it came positively and was largely greeted across, because it means faster development, especially in infrastructure and energy; recalled that in January 2024 the MCC team visited Liberia and gave the country authorization through the Ministry of Finance to recruit a coordinator, senior economist, private sector specialist and gender specialist for the program, totaling five vacancies, with a hundred Liberians applying: "Well, we don't have control over the American government and its democracy, as to what happened there. We have a new government in America. It's possible that the MCC may not be a priority at this stage. We can't continue to hope on the MCC. So, where we are now, unfortunately, everything that we started, we have to pause it. We will get over this, and we are getting over it"

a6105.speaker: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan, Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6105.name: Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan
a6105.title: Liberia's Minister of Finance and Development Planning
a6105.speech: Outlining domestic fiscal management and resource mobilization measures taken to address the gap, said government is currently attracting resources from other partners and raising domestic resources mobilization; disclosed that despite the MCC Compact pause Liberia is trying to implement the Liberia First Policy, focusing on key issues that will protect the nation's sovereignty and raise domestic revenue: "Now, last year, the country budget was in the amount of US$738 million. The domestic resources obligation we had was approximately US$690 million. The Liberia Revenue Authority and other revenue generation institutions raised US$698 million, which is eight hundred dollars more than targeted. Also, last year, domestic revenue was the highest ever in the country's history" ; "The LRA is about to introduce a technology program known as the payment switch, which will be installed at businesses so that receipts are generated. We are also thinking of changing case and plucking linkages. There will be more audits. Technology will be leverage; the net effect is that we are going to raise more money for ourselves, and it will help us. We are also in concession negotiations to attract the best value for Liberia"

a6105.speaker: Alice Albright, Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a6105.name: Alice Albright
a6105.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Millennium Challenge Corporation
a6105.speech: "MCC is proud of our longstanding history with Liberia and is enthusiastic about embarking on a new partnership to advance opportunities for the people of Liberia"

a6158.speaker: Public universities in Malawi
a6158.name: Public universities in Malawi
a6158.speech: Have ordered all students sponsored by USAID to drop out or seek other sources of funding if they want to remain in school.

a6158.speaker: Government of Malawi
a6158.name: Government of Malawi
a6158.speech: Malawi's government says it is working to ensure that students can continue their education.

a6158.speaker: James Mphande, communications manager at the Malawi University of Science and Technology (MUST)
a6158.name: James Mphande
a6158.title: communications manager at the Malawi University of Science and Technology (MUST)
a6158.speech: Said the U.S. foreign aid freeze is a big blow to several USAID-funded projects the school was implementing. "And what it means now is that everything has been suspended. So, if we were developing a curriculum, we can't proceed. If we had some outreach activities, we can't proceed. If we were in the process of making some procurements, we can't proceed."

a6158.speaker: James Mphande, communications manager at the Malawi University of Science and Technology (MUST)
a6158.name: James Mphande
a6158.title: communications manager at the Malawi University of Science and Technology (MUST)
a6158.speech: He said some sponsored students may face the impact next semester. "Fortunately, we are in the middle of a semester. So, probably fees or support for this semester was already sorted out. But for the upcoming semesters or years, it means the students will have to look elsewhere for support or they risk withdrawing."

a6158.speaker: Patience Yamikani Chakwana, first-year business information technology student at MUST and USAID beneficiary
a6158.name: Patience Yamikani Chakwana
a6158.title: first-year business information technology student at MUST and USAID beneficiary
a6158.speech: Told VOA that she is already feeling the impact. Chakwana said the foreign aid suspension was imposed before students received money for their daily upkeep. "It was really unexpected. It was, like, we have just started school after a week, then we are getting the news. At the time, we didn't have the money, and the pocket money had not been given. ... I heard the news while I was in class. I didn't know what to do. That was the only hope I had." Chakwana said USAID was paying for her tuition and accommodation, as well as giving her money for groceries and the internet connection for her mobile phone. She said she now survives on money she borrows from friends.

a6158.speaker: Jessie Kabwila, Malawi's Minister of Higher Education
a6158.name: Jessie Kabwila
a6158.title: Malawi's Minister of Higher Education
a6158.speech: Said the aid suspension is discouraging, but the Malawi government is working to find other sources to help students. "We have engaged local partnerships that are in the private sector to see how they can help us. We have also engaged international partners. For example, we have got a standing agreement with the Republic of Morocco. We have also engaged the Czech Republic, and we will be engaging others, too."

a6158.speaker: Alexander Kude, deputy director for the Commonwealth Students Association
a6158.name: Alexander Kude
a6158.title: deputy director for the Commonwealth Students Association
a6158.speech: Told VOA that the U.S. foreign aid suspension should be a wake-up call for developing countries to start investing more in education and reduce overdependence on foreign aid. "Look, the budget that the United States of America uses to fund us through USAID, it's just a percent of their money and budget. If you look how much that is and where they get it from, why not stand alone and do it ourselves?"

a6158.speaker: The Trump administration
a6158.name: The Trump administration
a6158.speech: Says it imposed the 90-day freeze to review USAID spending and make sure it aligns with U.S. policy and interests.

a6248.speaker: UN refugee agency (UNHCR)
a6248.name: UN refugee agency (UNHCR)
